steps.step: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment paper, then grease it well.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk the milk, egg, melted butter, and vanilla extract until smooth.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and stir just until combined — small lumps are fine, they smooth out as the pancake bakes.
Pour the batter onto the prepared sheet pan and spread it into an even layer — an even layer is what keeps a sheet pan pancake from browning in spots the way a skillet would.
Bake until the center springs back when lightly pressed and the edges turn golden, 12 to 14 minutes.
Let the pancake cool on the pan for 3 minutes, then slice into squares.
Brush the squares lightly with butter and serve warm, stacked or fanned out on a platter.
In a wide, shallow dish, whisk together the eggs, milk, cinnamon, vanilla extract, sugar, and salt.
Preheat the air fryer to 375°F for about 3 minutes — a hot basket is what gives the outside its crust.
Dip a slice of bread into the egg mixture, letting it soak for a few seconds per side until saturated but not falling apart.
Brush both sides of the soaked slice lightly with melted butter — a light coat is all an air fryer needs, unlike a skillet.
Lay the slices in a single layer in the air fryer basket, without overlapping, so hot air can reach every side.
Air fry until golden and set, about 5 minutes, then flip and cook the other side until deep golden brown, about 4 more minutes.
Repeat with the remaining bread in batches, brushing with more butter each time.
Serve hot, stacked and ready for your favorite toppings.
In a wide, shallow dish, whisk together the eggs, milk, cinnamon, vanilla extract, sugar, and salt.
Heat a griddle over medium heat and melt a tablespoon of the butter across the surface.
Dip a slice of bread into the egg mixture, soaking a few seconds per side until saturated but not falling apart.
Lay several soaked slices directly on the griddle at once — its flat, even surface means you can cook a full batch side by side instead of one pan at a time.
Cook until deep golden brown on the bottom, about 3 minutes.
Flip each slice and cook the second side until golden and the center feels set when pressed, about 3 minutes more.
Move the finished slices to a plate and repeat with the remaining bread, adding more butter to the griddle as needed.
Serve hot, stacked and ready for your favorite toppings.
In a wide, shallow dish, whisk together the eggs, milk, cinnamon, vanilla extract, sugar, and salt.
Heat the oven to 425°F and put a rimmed sheet pan inside to preheat — a hot pan gives the bread a head start on browning the way a hot skillet would.
Dip each slice of bread into the egg mixture, letting it soak for a few seconds per side until saturated but not falling apart.
Carefully remove the hot sheet pan, brush it with a little of the butter, and arrange the soaked slices in a single layer.
Bake for 10 minutes, then flip each slice and bake until deep golden on both sides, about 8 more minutes.
Move the slices to a plate and repeat with any remaining bread.
Serve hot, stacked and ready for your favorite toppings.
Grease a small loaf pan that fits inside your air fryer basket, about 6 inches long.
In a large bowl, mash the bananas with a fork until mostly smooth.
Stir the melted butter into the mashed bananas until combined.
Mix in the sugar, egg, and vanilla extract until smooth.
Sprinkle the baking soda and salt over the batter and stir them in.
Add the flour and stir just until no dry streaks remain — overmixing makes the loaf tough.

Pour the batter into the prepared pan, smooth the top, and preheat the air fryer to 320°F for 3 minutes — a lower temperature than an oven keeps the top from scorching before the center bakes through.
Set the pan in the air fryer basket and cook until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, 35 to 40 minutes, loosely tenting the top with foil halfway through if it's browning quickly.
Cool the loaf in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn it out onto a rack to cool completely before slicing.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
In another bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, melted butter, and vanilla extract until smooth.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir just until combined, with a few lumps remaining.
Toss the blueberries with a spoonful of the dry mix left in the bowl before folding them gently into the batter — this keeps them from sinking.
Divide the batter among greased silicone muffin cups, filling each about three-quarters full — silicone cups are easiest to lift out of a hot air fryer basket.
Preheat the air fryer to 320°F for 3 minutes, then arrange as many cups as fit in a single layer in the basket, leaving space between them for air to circulate.
Air fry until domed and golden and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, 10 to 12 minutes.
Let the muffins cool in the cups for 5 minutes before moving them to a rack.
Repeat preheating and air frying with the remaining batter until all the muffins are baked.
Cook the breakfast sausage in a skillet over medium heat, breaking it into small pieces, until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the diced potato to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until the edges turn golden, about 4 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, salt, and pepper, then pour into the skillet and cook, stirring gently, until just set, about 3 minutes.
Warm the tortillas briefly in a dry pan so they fold without cracking.
Divide the egg mixture and cheddar cheese among the tortillas, placing the filling just below the center.
Fold in the sides, then roll each tortilla up tightly into a burrito.
Preheat the air fryer to 375°F for 3 minutes, then place the burritos seam-side down in the basket so the seam seals as they cook.
Air fry until the tortilla is golden and crisp, about 6 minutes, flipping halfway through — this crisps the outside the way a dry skillet would, without needing added oil.
Let the burritos rest for a minute, then serve warm, or wrap tightly in foil to eat on the go.
Heat the oven to 375°F.
Warm the olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat and add the onion and bell pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, and paprika and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes, season with salt and pepper, and bring to a simmer.
Let the sauce simmer on the stovetop until it thickens slightly, about 8 minutes.
Use the back of a spoon to make 6 small wells in the sauce, then crack an egg into each one.

Slide the skillet into the oven and bake until the egg whites are set but the yolks are still soft, 8 to 10 minutes — the oven's steady, all-around heat sets the whites evenly without you needing to cover the pan.
Scatter the feta cheese and parsley over the top just before serving.
In a large bowl, toss together the rolled oats, almonds, cinnamon, and salt.
In a small bowl, whisk the maple syrup, vegetable oil, and vanilla extract together.
Pour the wet mixture over the oats and stir until every piece is coated.

Line the air fryer basket with a piece of parchment paper, poking a few holes in it so air still flows, and preheat the air fryer to 300°F for 3 minutes — a gentler temperature keeps granola from scorching in the tighter space of a basket.
Spread a third of the oat mixture in a thin, even layer in the basket — granola needs room to crisp, so work in batches rather than crowding it.
Air fry for 10 minutes, then shake the basket and stir the granola so the edges don't burn before the center catches up.
Continue air frying, checking and stirring every few minutes, until deep golden brown, 5 to 8 more minutes.
Slide the granola onto a plate to cool completely without stirring — this is when the clusters form — then repeat with the remaining batches.
Once all batches are cool, break the granola into clusters and mix in the dried cranberries before storing in an airtight container.
Shred the russet potatoes on the large holes of a box grater into a bowl of cold water.
Drain the shredded potatoes and squeeze them firmly in a clean kitchen towel to remove as much water as possible — the drier the shreds, the crisper they get without a deep pool of oil.
Toss the dried shreds with half the vegetable oil and season generously with salt and pepper.
Preheat the air fryer to 380°F for 3 minutes.
Divide the potatoes into two portions and press one portion into a thin, even patty directly in the air fryer basket.
Air fry until deeply golden and crisp on the bottom, about 10 minutes, then flip carefully with a spatula.
Brush the top with a little more of the remaining oil and air fry until crisp on the second side, about 6 more minutes.
Transfer to a plate and repeat with the remaining potatoes, then serve hot.
Shred the russet potatoes on the large holes of a box grater into a bowl of cold water.
Drain the shredded potatoes and squeeze them firmly in a clean kitchen towel to remove as much water as possible.
Toss the dried shreds with the vegetable oil and season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat the oven to 450°F and put a rimmed sheet pan in to preheat — starting the potatoes on a hot pan is what gives them a crisp bottom without a stovetop.
Carefully remove the hot sheet pan and spread the potatoes in a thin, even layer across the whole pan — the more room between shreds, the crispier they get.
Bake for 15 minutes, then flip the potatoes in sections with a spatula.
Bake until deeply golden and crisp, 10 to 12 more minutes.
Serve hot, straight off the pan.
Preheat the air fryer to 370°F for 3 minutes.
Lay the bacon flat in the air fryer basket in a single layer and air fry until crisp, 7 to 9 minutes, flipping halfway — no added oil needed, the fat renders on its own.
Move the bacon to a paper towel-lined plate.
Crack the egg into a small oven-safe ramekin that fits in the basket, season with salt and pepper, and gently break the yolk.
Air fry the egg until the white is just set, about 4 minutes.
Top the egg with the cheddar cheese and air fry 1 more minute, just until melted.
Meanwhile, spread the bread lightly with butter and air fry alongside, cut-side up, until toasted, about 3 minutes.
Stack the bacon and cheesy egg between the toasted bread and serve warm.
Combine the eggs, cottage cheese, and milk in a blender and blend until smooth and frothy.
Season the mixture with salt and pepper.
Divide the spinach, bell pepper, and cheddar cheese evenly among the cups of a silicone egg bite mold.
Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables, filling each cup about two-thirds full.
Preheat the air fryer to 300°F for 3 minutes — a gentler temperature than an oven keeps these custardy instead of rubbery.
Set the mold in the air fryer basket and cook until puffed and set in the center, 12 to 14 minutes.
Let them cool for a few minutes before running a knife around the edges to loosen, then repeat with any remaining batter.
Combine the eggs, cottage cheese, and milk in a blender and blend until smooth and frothy.
Season the mixture with salt and pepper.
Divide the spinach, bell pepper, and cheddar cheese evenly among the cups of a silicone egg bite mold.
Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables, filling each cup about two-thirds full, then cover the mold tightly with foil so condensation doesn't drip in as it steams.
Pour 1 cup of water into the pressure cooker insert and set the trivet inside, then place the mold on top.
Lock the lid, seal the valve, and cook on high pressure for 8 minutes, allowing a few extra minutes for the pot to come to pressure before the timer starts.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes before opening the lid — a slow release keeps the custard from deflating the way a quick release would.
Carefully lift out the mold, let it cool for a few minutes, then run a knife around the edges to release the egg bites.
Grease a 7-inch round pan that fits inside your pressure cooker.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 4 minutes.
Add the spinach and cook just until wilted, about 1 minute, then spread the mixture in the bottom of the prepared pan.
Scatter the swiss cheese over the vegetables.
In a bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, heavy cream, nutmeg, salt, and pepper until well combined.
Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables and cheese, then cover the pan tightly with foil so condensation doesn't drip in as it steams.
Pour 1 1/2 cups of water into the pressure cooker insert, set the trivet inside, and lower the pan onto the trivet using a foil sling.
Lock the lid, seal the valve, and cook on high pressure for 22 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then carefully lift out the pan — a natural release keeps the custard from sinking in the center the way a quick release can.
Let the quiche rest for 10 minutes before slicing so it holds together.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt, and pepper together in a bowl.
Melt the butter in a nonstick skillet over medium heat and scramble the eggs until just set, about 3 minutes. Slide them onto a plate.
Lay one tortilla flat and sprinkle half the cheddar cheese over one half, then top with the scrambled eggs and the rest of the cheese.
Fold the empty half of the tortilla over the filling and press down gently.
Preheat the air fryer to 370°F for 3 minutes.
Lightly brush or spray both sides of the folded quesadilla and set it in the air fryer basket.
Air fry until golden and crisp, about 8 minutes, flipping halfway through — the air fryer crisps both sides at once, so there's no need to babysit a flip in a hot pan.
Repeat with the second tortilla, then slice each into wedges and serve with salsa.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt, and pepper together in a bowl.
Melt the butter on a griddle set over medium heat and scramble the eggs until just set, about 3 minutes. Slide them to one side of the griddle.
Lay a tortilla flat on the open side of the griddle, sprinkle half the cheddar cheese over one half, then top with the scrambled eggs and the rest of the cheese.
Fold the empty half of the tortilla over the filling and press down gently with a spatula.

Cook until golden and crisp on the bottom, about 2 minutes, then flip and crisp the other side, about 2 minutes more — a griddle's wide, flat surface makes it easy to cook both quesadillas side by side.
Repeat with the second tortilla using the same open space on the griddle.
Slice each quesadilla into wedges and serve with salsa.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
Cut the cold butter into the flour with your fingers or a pastry cutter until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs with some pea-sized pieces.
Pour in the buttermilk and stir just until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface, pat it into a 1-inch-thick round, and cut into biscuits with a cutter or glass.
Preheat the air fryer to 330°F for 3 minutes, then arrange the biscuits in the basket with space between them — they need room for air to circulate and rise evenly.
Air fry until golden on top and cooked through, 10 to 12 minutes, checking a couple minutes early since air fryers run hotter than ovens.
While the biscuits cook, cook the breakfast sausage in a skillet over medium heat, breaking it up, until browned, about 6 minutes.
Sprinkle the gravy thickener over the sausage and stir for 1 minute to cook off the raw flour taste.
Slowly pour in the whole milk while stirring, then simmer until thickened, about 5 minutes.
Season the gravy generously with black pepper, split the warm biscuits, and spoon the gravy over the top to serve.
Grease the inside of the slow cooker insert and spread the cubed bread evenly across the bottom.
In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, heavy cream, sugar, vanilla extract, and cinnamon until smooth.
Pour the egg mixture evenly over the bread cubes, pressing down gently so every piece gets soaked.
Drizzle the melted butter over the top.
Sprinkle the streusel topping evenly over the surface.

Cover and cook on low for 4 to 5 hours, until the center is set and a knife inserted comes out clean — a slow cooker's gentle, even heat does the same custard-soaking work as the oven, just slower, so there's no need to soak the bread ahead of time.
Turn off the slow cooker and let the casserole rest with the lid ajar for 10 minutes — this lets the top firm up a bit since a slow cooker won't crisp it the way an oven does.
Scoop into bowls and serve warm.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, salt, and pepper until fully combined.
Stir in the ham, bell pepper, and green onion.
Preheat the air fryer to 320°F for 3 minutes and grease a silicone muffin tray that fits inside the basket.
Divide the mixture evenly among the muffin cups, filling each about two-thirds full.
Sprinkle the cheddar cheese over the top of each cup.
Set the tray in the air fryer basket and cook until puffed and set in the center, 12 to 14 minutes.
Let the egg cups cool for a few minutes before running a knife around the edges to lift them out, then repeat with any remaining batter.
Pat the chicken breasts dry, season both sides with salt and pepper, and dust lightly with the flour, shaking off the excess.

Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and sear the chicken until golden, about 3 minutes per side — it won't cook through yet, but the color adds flavor the slow cooker can't build on its own.
Transfer the chicken to the slow cooker.
Add the garlic, sun-dried tomatoes, and italian seasoning to the slow cooker.
Pour in only half the chicken broth — a slow cooker doesn't let liquid evaporate the way a stovetop pan does, so less keeps the sauce from turning thin.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken is cooked through with no pink in the center, 3 to 4 hours.
Stir in the heavy cream and parmesan during the last 15 minutes of cooking — adding dairy late keeps it from separating over a long, slow cook.
Scatter the basil over the top just before serving.
Pat the chicken breasts dry, season both sides with salt and pepper, and dust lightly with the flour, shaking off the excess.

Heat a grill to medium-high and oil the grates. Grill the chicken until deep grill marks form and it releases easily, about 5 minutes per side, then move it to a plate — it will finish cooking in the sauce later.
Set a skillet directly on the grill grates over the cooler side of the grill, add the olive oil, and cook the garlic just until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Pour in the chicken broth and scrape up any browned bits in the skillet.
Stir in the heavy cream, sun-dried tomatoes, and italian seasoning, and let the sauce bubble gently over the grill's indirect heat until it thickens slightly, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the parmesan until melted and smooth.

Return the chicken to the skillet, spoon sauce over the top, close the grill lid, and cook until the chicken is cooked through with no pink in the center, about 8 minutes — the closed lid turns the grill into an oven for this last step.
Scatter the basil over the top just before serving.
Pat the chicken breasts dry, season both sides with salt and pepper, and dust lightly with the flour, shaking off the excess.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, heat the olive oil, and sear the chicken until golden, about 3 minutes per side. Move it to a plate.
Add the garlic to the pot and stir just until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Pour in only half the chicken broth and scrape up the browned bits — a pressure cooker needs less liquid than a skillet since none evaporates during cooking.
Stir in the sun-dried tomatoes and italian seasoning, then return the chicken to the pot.
Lock the lid, seal the valve, and cook on high pressure for 8 minutes.
Quick release the pressure so the chicken doesn't overcook, then carefully open the lid.

Switch back to sauté, stir in the heavy cream and parmesan, and simmer until the sauce thickens slightly, about 4 minutes — this happens after pressure cooking since dairy can scorch or separate under high pressure.
Scatter the basil over the top just before serving.
Warm the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion, stirring often, until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the curry powder and stir constantly for 30 seconds to toast the spices — do this in the skillet, not the slow cooker, since dry heat is what wakes up ground spices.
Scrape the onion mixture into the slow cooker.
Add the chicken, diced tomatoes, and only half the coconut milk — a slow cooker traps moisture instead of simmering it off, so extra liquid would leave the sauce thin.
Add the salt and stir to coat every piece of chicken in sauce.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken is fall-apart tender, 5 to 6 hours.
Stir in the remaining coconut milk during the last 15 minutes of cooking to freshen the sauce's richness.
Taste and adjust the salt, then scatter the cilantro over the top before serving.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, warm the vegetable oil, and cook the onion, stirring often, until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the curry powder and stir constantly for 30 seconds to toast the spices.
Pour in the diced tomatoes and only half the coconut milk, scraping up any browned bits — a pressure cooker needs less liquid since nothing evaporates under a sealed lid.
Add the chicken and salt and stir to coat.
Lock the lid, seal the valve, and cook on high pressure for 8 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then quick release any remaining pressure — the rest time keeps the chicken from turning stringy under a sudden release.
Stir in the remaining coconut milk and simmer on sauté for a couple minutes to bring the sauce together.
Taste and adjust the salt, then scatter the cilantro over the top before serving.
Stir together the chicken thighs, yogurt, and half the garam masala in a bowl, and let it marinate at least 15 minutes — this tenderizes the meat before it goes into the slow cooker.

Melt half the butter in a skillet over medium-high heat and brown the marinated chicken on all sides, about 5 minutes — a slow cooker never browns anything on its own, so this stovetop sear is where the deep flavor comes from.
Add the remaining butter to the skillet and cook the onion until soft and golden, about 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic, ginger, and remaining garam masala until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Transfer the browned chicken and the onion mixture to the slow cooker, then pour in the tomato puree and salt and stir to combine.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken is fall-apart tender, about 6 hours (or on high for about 3 hours).
Stir in the heavy cream during the last 15 minutes of cooking — adding it any earlier can make it break over the long, steady heat.
Scatter the cilantro over the top before serving.
Stir together the chicken thighs, yogurt, and half the garam masala in a bowl, and let it marinate at least 30 minutes — a grill wants bold flavor already built in before the heat hits.
Heat the grill to medium-high and clean the grates well so the marinated chicken releases easily.
Grill the chicken, turning once, until lightly charred at the edges and cooked through with no pink in the center, about 10 minutes total.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft and golden, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, and remaining garam masala and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Pour in the tomato puree and salt and simmer until slightly thickened, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the heavy cream, then add the grilled chicken to the skillet and simmer 3 minutes so it soaks up the sauce.
Scatter the cilantro over the top before serving.
Stir together the chicken thighs, yogurt, and half the garam masala in a bowl, and let it marinate at least 15 minutes.
Set the pot to sauté, melt half the butter, and brown the chicken on the outside, about 5 minutes — it does not need to cook through yet.
Move the chicken to a plate, add the remaining butter, and cook the onion until soft and golden, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, and remaining garam masala and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Pour in the tomato puree and salt, return the chicken and any juices, and stir, then lock the lid and set the vent to sealing.
Pressure cook on high for 8 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes before opening the vent — a slow release keeps the chicken juicy instead of turning it tough.
Switch the pot back to sauté and stir in the heavy cream, simmering about 2 minutes until warmed through — adding cream now, instead of under pressure, keeps it from curdling.
Scatter the cilantro over the top before serving.
Toss the chicken breast with the chili powder, cumin, paprika, salt, and half the vegetable oil in a bowl until evenly coated.
Toss the bell peppers and onion with the remaining vegetable oil in a separate bowl.
Heat the grill to medium-high and clean the grates well so nothing sticks.
Grill the chicken directly on the grates, turning once, until nicely charred and cooked through with no pink in the center, about 12 minutes total.
Grill the peppers and onion alongside — a grill basket keeps the slices from falling through — turning occasionally, until softened and charred at the edges, about 10 minutes.
Move the chicken to a cutting board to rest a few minutes, then slice into strips.
Toss the sliced chicken with the grilled vegetables and squeeze the lime juice over everything.
Warm the tortillas on the grill for a few seconds per side, then serve alongside the chicken and vegetables for building your own fajitas.
Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the chicken breast with the chili powder, cumin, paprika, salt, and half the vegetable oil in a bowl.
Toss the bell peppers and onion with the remaining vegetable oil and spread them over a sheet pan.
Add the chicken to the sheet pan in a single layer alongside the vegetables — giving everything room, instead of crowding it, is what lets it char instead of steam.
Roast until the chicken is cooked through with no pink in the center and the vegetables are tender with lightly charred edges, about 20 minutes, stirring once halfway through.
During the last few minutes of roasting, wrap the tortillas in foil and warm them in the oven.
Squeeze the lime juice over the sheet pan and toss everything together, then serve with the warm tortillas for building your own fajitas.
Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Set up three shallow dishes: one with flour, one with the beaten eggs, and one with the breadcrumbs mixed with half the parmesan.
Dredge each chicken breast in flour, then egg, then the breadcrumb mixture, pressing gently so the coating sticks.
Preheat the air fryer to 375°F — starting hot is what gives the coating its crunch.
Brush both sides of the breaded chicken lightly with the olive oil, standing in for the oil a skillet would normally provide, and place it in the air fryer basket in a single layer without crowding.
Air fry until golden and crisp, flipping halfway through, about 12 minutes.
Spoon the marinara sauce over each piece, then top with the mozzarella and remaining parmesan.
Return to the air fryer and cook until the chicken is cooked through with no pink in the center and the cheese is melted and bubbling, about 4 minutes.
Let rest a couple of minutes, then scatter the basil over the top before serving.
Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper on both sides — for the grill, skip the breading altogether, since a coated crust would just burn and fall through the grates.
Heat the grill to medium-high and clean the grates well.
Brush the chicken lightly with the olive oil to keep it from sticking.
Grill the chicken, turning once, until nicely marked and cooked through with no pink in the center, about 10 minutes total.
Spoon the marinara sauce over each piece, then top with the mozzarella and remaining parmesan.
Close the grill lid and cook just until the cheese is melted and bubbling, about 3 minutes — the closed lid works like a little oven.
Move to a platter, let rest a couple of minutes, then scatter the basil over the top before serving.
Take the chicken out of the fridge while you prep so it is not ice-cold when it goes in.
Pat the chicken completely dry inside and out with paper towels — this is the secret to crisp skin, especially in an air fryer’s smaller space.
Stuff the cavity with the lemon, garlic, rosemary, thyme, and onion.
Rub the softened butter all over the outside of the chicken, then season generously with salt and pepper.
Tie the legs together with kitchen twine and tuck the wings under so the chicken sits compactly — a snug shape matters more here since basket space is tight.
Preheat the air fryer to 360°F.
Place the chicken breast-side down in the air fryer basket and cook for 30 minutes.
Flip the chicken breast-side up and continue cooking until the skin is deep golden and a thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F, about 30 more minutes.
Let the chicken rest for 10 minutes before carving — this keeps the juices in the meat instead of on the cutting board.
Take the chicken out of the fridge to lose its chill.
Pat the chicken completely dry inside and out with paper towels.
Stuff the cavity with the lemon, garlic, rosemary, and thyme.
Rub the softened butter all over the outside, then season generously with salt and pepper.
Line the bottom of the slow cooker with the quartered onion and set the chicken on top, breast-side up — this keeps the chicken out of its own juices instead of stewing at the bottom.
Cover and cook on low until a thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F and the meat is fall-apart tender, about 5 hours (or on high for about 3 hours).
Carefully lift the chicken onto a baking sheet and, if you like a browned finish, run it under the broiler for a few minutes until the skin deepens in color — the slow cooker alone will not crisp it.
Let the chicken rest for 10 minutes before carving.
Take the chicken out of the fridge to lose its chill.
Pat the chicken completely dry inside and out with paper towels.
Stuff the cavity with the lemon, garlic, rosemary, and thyme.
Rub the softened butter all over the outside, then season generously with salt and pepper.
Place a trivet in the pressure cooker, pour in a cup of water, and set the chicken on the trivet breast-side up.
Lock the lid, set the vent to sealing, and pressure cook on high for 25 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 15 minutes before opening the vent the rest of the way — a natural release keeps a whole bird from tearing at the joints.
Check that a thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F; if it needs a touch more, seal and cook a few minutes longer.
For crisp, browned skin, transfer the chicken to a baking sheet and run it under the broiler for a few minutes — the pressure cooker keeps it tender but will not brown it.
Let the chicken rest for 10 minutes before carving.

Warm the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion, carrots, and celery until just beginning to soften, about 4 minutes — a quick head start here builds more flavor than the slow cooker can on its own.
Stir in the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Transfer the vegetables to the slow cooker, add the chicken breasts whole, pour in the chicken broth, and season with salt and pepper.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender, about 6 hours (or on high for about 3 hours).
Lift the chicken onto a cutting board, shred it with two forks, and return it to the slow cooker.
Stir in the egg noodles, cover, and cook on high until tender, about 20 minutes — added any earlier, they would turn to mush over the long cook.
Taste and adjust the salt and pepper, then stir in the parsley before serving.
Set the pot to sauté, warm the olive oil, and cook the onion, carrots, and celery until just beginning to soften, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add the chicken breasts, pour in the chicken broth, and season with salt and pepper.
Lock the lid, set the vent to sealing, and pressure cook on high for 10 minutes.
Quick release the pressure — soup does not need the gentler natural release since there is no delicate meat structure to protect.
Lift the chicken out onto a cutting board, shred it with two forks, and return it to the pot.
Set the pot back to sauté, stir in the egg noodles, and cook until tender, about 8 minutes.
Taste and adjust the salt and pepper, then stir in the parsley before serving.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion, carrots, and celery until just beginning to soften, about 4 minutes.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir constantly for 1 minute to cook off the raw taste before it all goes into the slow cooker.
Transfer the vegetables to the slow cooker, add the chicken breasts, pour in the chicken broth, and season with salt and pepper.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken is tender and cooked through, about 5 hours (or on high for about 2.5 hours).
Lift the chicken onto a cutting board, shred or cube it, and return it to the slow cooker along with the milk and frozen peas, stirring until the sauce is thickened and creamy, about 15 minutes.

Near the end of cooking, heat the oven to 400°F, unroll the pie crusts onto a baking sheet, and bake until deep golden and flaky, about 15 minutes — the slow cooker keeps the filling creamy, so the crust gets its crunch entirely on its own.
Break the baked crust into large pieces and set a piece over each bowl of filling to serve.
Set the pot to sauté, melt the butter, and cook the onion, carrots, and celery until just beginning to soften, about 4 minutes.
Add the chicken breasts, pour in the chicken broth, and season with salt and pepper.
Lock the lid, set the vent to sealing, and pressure cook on high for 8 minutes.
Quick release the pressure, opening the vent carefully since the steam will be hot.
Lift the chicken onto a cutting board and cube or shred it.

Whisk the flour with a splash of the milk in a small bowl until smooth, set the pot to sauté, and stir the mixture in along with the remaining milk and the peas, simmering until thickened enough to coat the back of a spoon, about 4 minutes.
Return the chicken to the pot and stir to combine.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 400°F, unroll the pie crusts onto a baking sheet, and bake until deep golden and flaky, about 15 minutes.
Break the baked crust into pieces and set one over each bowl of filling to serve.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion, carrots, and celery until softened, about 6 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook, stirring occasionally, until no longer pink on the outside, about 6 minutes.
Sprinkle the flour over everything and stir constantly for 1 minute to cook off the raw taste.

Slowly pour in the chicken broth and milk, stirring constantly, and simmer until thickened enough to coat the back of a spoon, about 8 minutes — a little longer than usual, since there is no oven to help finish the chicken.
Stir in the frozen peas, season with salt and pepper, and simmer until the chicken is fully cooked through with no pink in the center, about 5 minutes.
While the filling finishes, cut the pie crusts into wide strips and cook them in a dry skillet over medium heat, flipping once, until puffed, flaky, and golden on both sides, about 6 minutes total.
Break the crust strips into pieces and scatter them over each bowl of filling just before serving so they stay crisp.
Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper on both sides.

Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and sear the chicken just until golden on both sides, about 4 minutes total — it will not cook through yet, but the color it picks up here is flavor the slow cooker cannot add on its own.
Transfer the chicken to the slow cooker with the garlic and only half the chicken broth — a slow cooker does not let liquid evaporate, so less goes further.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken is cooked through with no pink in the center, about 4 hours (or on high for about 2 hours).
Stir in the heavy cream, parmesan, and sun-dried tomatoes, and cook on high, uncovered, until slightly thickened, about 15 minutes.
Add the spinach and stir just until wilted, about 5 minutes.
Spoon the sauce over the chicken and serve.
Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper on both sides.
Set the pot to sauté, heat the olive oil, and sear the chicken until golden on both sides, about 5 minutes total.
Add the garlic and half the chicken broth — a pressure cooker needs some liquid to build steam, but not as much as a skillet since nothing evaporates — and scrape up any browned bits.
Lock the lid, set the vent to sealing, and pressure cook on high for 8 minutes.
Quick release the pressure.

Move the chicken to a plate, set the pot to sauté, and stir in the heavy cream, parmesan, and sun-dried tomatoes, simmering until slightly thickened, about 4 minutes — adding the cream after pressure cooking keeps it from curdling.
Add the spinach and stir just until wilted, about 1 minute.
Return the chicken to the pot, spoon the sauce over the top, and warm through before serving.
Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and sear the chicken just until golden, about 3 minutes per side — it will finish cooking in the slow cooker.
Place the chicken in the slow cooker with the butter and garlic.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken is fully cooked through with no pink in the center, about 3 hours (or on high for about 1.5 hours).
Move the chicken to a cutting board and slice it, then stir the heavy cream and parmesan into the slow cooker until the sauce is smooth, about 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the fettuccine according to the package until just tender, about 10 minutes, then drain — pasta turns to mush if it sits in the slow cooker for hours, so it is cooked separately and added at the end.
Stir the drained fettuccine into the sauce until coated, then top with the sliced chicken.
Scatter the parsley over the top before serving.
Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Heat the grill to medium-high and clean the grates well.
Brush the chicken lightly with the olive oil and grill, turning once, until nicely marked and cooked through with no pink in the center, about 12 minutes total.
Move the chicken to a cutting board to rest, then slice.
Meanwhile, bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the fettuccine according to the package until just tender, about 10 minutes. Drain, reserving a cup of the pasta water.
In a skillet, melt the butter over medium heat and cook the garlic until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Pour in the heavy cream and simmer gently, stirring often, about 3 minutes.
Whisk in the parmesan until smooth, thinning with a splash of the reserved pasta water if it looks too thick.
Add the drained fettuccine to the sauce and toss until every strand is coated.
Top with the grilled, sliced chicken and scatter the parsley over everything before serving.
Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Set the pot to sauté, heat the olive oil, and cook the chicken until golden on both sides, about 6 minutes total — it will finish cooking along with the pasta.
Move the chicken to a plate, add the butter and garlic to the pot, and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds.

Break the fettuccine in half, add it to the pot in a crisscross pattern, and pour in just enough water to submerge it, about 2 cups — this stands in for the boiling pot, since the pressure cooker can cook the noodles directly.
Nestle the chicken back on top of the pasta, lock the lid, set the vent to sealing, and pressure cook on high for 5 minutes.
Quick release the pressure.
Move the chicken to a cutting board to rest, then slice.

Set the pot to sauté and stir in the heavy cream and parmesan, tossing with the pasta until the sauce turns silky and coats every strand, about 3 minutes — adding the dairy after pressure cooking keeps it from scorching on the bottom.
Top with the sliced chicken and scatter the parsley over everything before serving.
In a bowl, toss the shredded chicken with the chili powder, cumin, and salt until evenly coated.
Lay out half the tortillas and scatter the cheddar cheese, seasoned chicken, and bell pepper evenly over each, then top with the remaining tortillas.
Preheat the air fryer to 370°F.
Brush both sides of each quesadilla lightly with the melted butter — this crisps the tortilla the way the skillet’s butter normally would.
Place one or two quesadillas in the air fryer basket in a single layer, without overlapping.
Air fry until the tortilla is golden and crisp and the cheese is fully melted, flipping halfway through, about 8 minutes.
Repeat with any remaining quesadillas.
Slice each quesadilla into wedges and serve while the cheese is still stretchy.
In a bowl, toss the shredded chicken with the chili powder, cumin, and salt until evenly coated.
Lay out half the tortillas and scatter the cheddar cheese, seasoned chicken, and bell pepper evenly over each, then top with the remaining tortillas.
Heat the griddle over medium heat and melt a little of the butter across the surface.
Place as many quesadillas as fit in a single layer on the hot griddle — the flat, wide surface means you can cook several at once instead of one at a time.
Cook until the bottom is golden and crisp, about 3 minutes, then carefully flip and cook the other side until golden and the cheese is fully melted, about 3 minutes more.
Add a little more butter to the griddle and repeat with any remaining quesadillas.
Slice each quesadilla into wedges and serve while the cheese is still stretchy.
Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper.

Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and brown the chicken on the outside, about 4 minutes — it will not be cooked through yet, but this is where the flavor comes from since the slow cooker cannot brown anything.
Whisk together the garlic, honey, soy sauce, and rice vinegar in a small bowl, then pour it over the browned chicken in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken is fall-apart tender, about 4 hours (or on high for about 2 hours).
Whisk the cornstarch with a tablespoon of water in a small bowl until smooth, then stir it into the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on high until the sauce thickens into a glossy glaze that coats the chicken, about 15 minutes.
Scatter the green onion over the top before serving.
Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper, then toss with the cornstarch until lightly coated — the cornstarch helps the glaze cling once it hits the grill.
Whisk together the garlic, honey, soy sauce, and rice vinegar in a small bowl to make the glaze.
Heat the grill to medium and clean the grates well — medium, not high, since the honey in the glaze burns quickly over direct high heat.
Brush the chicken lightly with the vegetable oil and grill, turning occasionally, until mostly cooked through, about 8 minutes.

Brush the glaze over the chicken and continue grilling, turning and brushing once more, until cooked through with no pink inside and the glaze is sticky and slightly charred at the edges, about 4 minutes — brushing it on late keeps the sugars from scorching.
Move the chicken to a platter and scatter the green onion over the top before serving.
Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper.
Set the pot to sauté, heat the vegetable oil, and brown the chicken on the outside, about 4 minutes.
Push the chicken to one side, add the garlic to the empty space, and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Whisk together the honey, soy sauce, and rice vinegar in a small bowl, then pour it over the chicken.
Lock the lid, set the vent to sealing, and pressure cook on high for 5 minutes.
Quick release the pressure.
Whisk the cornstarch with a tablespoon of water in a small bowl until smooth, set the pot to sauté, and stir in the slurry, simmering until the sauce thickens into a glossy glaze, about 3 minutes.
Scatter the green onion over the top before serving.
Heat the oven to 425°F.
Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper, then toss with the cornstarch until lightly coated.
Toss the chicken with the vegetable oil and spread it in a single layer on a sheet pan — giving it room is what lets it brown instead of steam.
Roast until the chicken is mostly cooked through, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk together the garlic, honey, soy sauce, and rice vinegar in a small bowl.
Spoon the glaze over the chicken and return it to the oven until cooked through with no pink inside and the glaze is bubbling and slightly caramelized, about 8 minutes.
Scatter the green onion over the top before serving.
Heat a flat-top griddle over medium-high heat and drizzle on half the vegetable oil, letting it spread and shimmer across the surface.

Season the chicken breast with salt and pepper, spread it in a thin layer on the hot griddle, and cook without moving it too much until golden and cooked through, about 5 minutes. Push it to a cooler edge of the griddle.
Pour the beaten eggs onto a clear patch of the griddle and scramble with your spatulas, chopping them into small curds as they set, about 1 minute, then mix them into the chicken.
Drizzle on the remaining vegetable oil, scatter the frozen peas and carrots in a thin layer, and cook, tossing occasionally, until thawed and lightly blistered, about 3 minutes.
Clear a small hot spot on the griddle, add the garlic, and chop it into the surface with your spatula until fragrant, about 30 seconds, then stir it through the vegetables.

Spread the cold rice across the griddle in a thin, even layer, let it sit undisturbed for a minute to pick up a light char on the bottom, then chop and flip it constantly until heated through, about 5 minutes.
Push the rice, chicken, and vegetables together into one pile, drizzle the soy sauce and sesame oil over the top, and toss everything with your spatulas until glossy and evenly coated.
Scatter the green onion over the top and serve straight from the griddle while it is hot.
In a bowl, stir together the chicken thighs, yogurt, half the garam masala, and the paprika, and let it marinate for at least 20 minutes — longer is fine, since the slow cooker forgives timing.
Heat half the vegetable oil in a skillet over high heat and sear the marinated chicken just until charred at the edges, about 5 minutes — this is the only browning the dish gets, so don't skip it.
Transfer the chicken to the slow cooker. In the same skillet, add the remaining oil and cook the onion until soft and golden, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, and remaining garam masala and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute, then scrape the onion mixture into the slow cooker with the chicken.
Add the tomato puree and salt to the slow cooker and stir everything together.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken is fork-tender and the sauce is fragrant, about 6 hours (or on high for about 3 hours) — the gentle heat does what a stovetop simmer would, just slower.

Stir in the heavy cream during the last 15 minutes with the lid off — a slow cooker won't reduce the sauce the way a skillet does, so adding the cream late and letting steam escape keeps it from turning watery.
Scatter the cilantro over the top before serving.
In a bowl, stir together the chicken thighs, yogurt, half the garam masala, and the paprika, and let it marinate for at least 20 minutes.
Heat the grill to medium-high heat and oil the grates well so the marinated chicken releases cleanly.
Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, until charred in spots and cooked through with no pink in the center, about 10 minutes total — real fire char is something a skillet can only approximate.
Meanwhile, warm half the vegetable oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion, stirring occasionally, until soft and golden, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, and remaining garam masala and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Pour in the tomato puree and salt, bring to a simmer, and cook until slightly thickened, about 10 minutes.

Stir in the heavy cream, then add the grilled chicken and any juices, and simmer gently just to bring everything together, about 3 minutes — the chicken is already cooked through from the grill, so this is only for marrying flavors.
Scatter the cilantro over the top before serving.
In a bowl, stir together the chicken thighs, yogurt, half the garam masala, and the paprika, and let it marinate for at least 20 minutes while you prep everything else.

Set the pressure cooker to saute, add half the vegetable oil, and sear the marinated chicken in batches until charred at the edges, about 5 minutes. Remove to a plate — it will finish cooking under pressure.
Add the remaining oil and cook the onion, stirring often since the saute function runs hot near the edges, until soft and golden, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, and remaining garam masala and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Pour in the tomato puree and salt, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom, then return the chicken and its juices to the pot.
Lock the lid, seal the valve, and cook on high pressure for 8 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then quick-release whatever remains — natural release keeps the chicken from turning tough.
Stir in the heavy cream — pressure cooking would curdle it, so it goes in only after the lid is off — then scatter the cilantro over the top before serving.
In a bowl, stir together the chicken thighs, yogurt, half the garam masala, and the paprika, and let it marinate for at least 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 450 degrees and drizzle half the vegetable oil over a rimmed sheet pan.

Spread the marinated chicken and the onion in a single layer on the sheet pan and roast until the chicken is charred in spots and the onion is soft, about 15 minutes — the high dry heat stands in for the pan-sear without you standing over a skillet.
Meanwhile, warm the remaining oil in a saucepan over medium heat, add the garlic, ginger, and remaining garam masala, and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Pour in the tomato puree and salt, bring to a simmer, and cook until slightly thickened, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the heavy cream, then scrape the roasted chicken and onion, along with any pan juices, into the sauce.
Simmer gently until everything is heated through and the chicken shows no pink in the center, about 5 minutes.
Scatter the cilantro over the top before serving.
Pat the chicken thighs dry and toss them with the olive oil, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.
Preheat the air fryer to 380 degrees — starting from hot air is what gets the skin crackling instead of steaming.
Arrange the thighs skin-side down in a single layer in the air fryer basket, leaving space between each so air can circulate, and cook for 10 minutes.
Flip the thighs skin-side up and cook until the skin is deeply golden and a thermometer reads 165 degrees, about 12 more minutes.

Brush the bbq sauce generously over each thigh and cook until the sauce is set and sticky, about 4 more minutes — air fryers run hot and fast, so watch closely since the sugar in the sauce can scorch if left too long.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes before serving so the glaze can set.
Pat the chicken thighs dry and toss them with the olive oil, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.
Lay the chicken thighs in the slow cooker in a single layer, skin-side up — the skin won't crisp here, but leaving it on keeps the meat basted as it cooks.
Pour half the bbq sauce over the thighs, saving the rest for later — a slow cooker won't reduce the sauce, so holding some back keeps it from getting thin and watery.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken is fork-tender and pulls easily from the bone, about 6 hours (or on high for about 3 hours).

Brush the remaining bbq sauce over the thighs, then cook uncovered on high for 15 minutes so the sauce thickens into a glaze — cracking the lid lets the extra moisture escape since the pot itself won't reduce it.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes before serving so the glaze can set.
Season the chicken breasts on both sides with salt and pepper.
Preheat the air fryer to 375 degrees and lightly brush the basket with a little of the olive oil so the chicken doesn't stick.
Place the chicken breasts in a single layer in the basket and cook, flipping halfway, until golden and a thermometer reads 165 degrees, about 16 minutes.
Meanwhile, warm the remaining olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat, add the garlic, and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Pour in the chicken broth and lemon juice and simmer until slightly reduced, about 3 minutes.
Add the lemon slices and thyme and simmer 1 minute more.
Remove from the heat and swirl in the butter until the sauce turns glossy.
Slice the air-fried chicken if you like, spoon the warm lemon sauce over the top, and serve right away while the chicken is still crackly from the basket.
Season the chicken breasts on both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat the grill to medium-high heat and oil the grates so the chicken releases cleanly.
Grill the chicken until deep grill marks form on the first side, about 6 minutes, then flip.

Meanwhile, melt the butter with the remaining olive oil, garlic, and thyme in a small saucepan over low heat just until fragrant, about 1 minute, then stir in the lemon juice — this becomes a baste, since the grill won't build a pan sauce for you.

Brush the chicken generously with the lemon-herb butter as it finishes grilling, and lay the lemon slices on the grates alongside it to soften and lightly char, about 6 more minutes, until the chicken reaches 165 degrees with no pink in the center.
Pour the chicken broth into the now-empty baste pan and swirl over low heat to loosen any bits, warming it into a thin finishing sauce.
Move the chicken to a platter, spoon the warm broth sauce and grilled lemon slices over the top, and let it rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Heat the oven to 425 degrees.
Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper and arrange them on a sheet pan, drizzled with the olive oil.
Scatter the garlic and thyme over the chicken and tuck the lemon slices around it.

Roast until the chicken reaches 165 degrees with no pink in the center, about 20 minutes — the sheet pan's dry heat won't build a pan sauce like a skillet does, so a quick one gets made separately while it roasts.
Meanwhile, warm the chicken broth and lemon juice in a small saucepan over medium heat and simmer until lightly reduced, about 4 minutes.
Remove from the heat and swirl in the butter until glossy.
Spoon the warm sauce over the roasted chicken along with the softened roasted lemon slices, and serve.
In a bowl, mix the shredded chicken with 1 cup of the cheddar cheese, the onion, cumin, salt, and a little of the enchilada sauce.
Spread a thin layer of enchilada sauce in the bottom of the slow cooker.

Tear the tortillas into large pieces and layer about a third of them over the sauce, tearing to fit the round crock — rolling would collapse over hours of cooking, so this becomes a layered casserole instead, like a slow-cooker lasagna.
Spoon half the chicken filling over the tortillas and drizzle with a little enchilada sauce, then repeat with another layer of torn tortillas and the rest of the filling.
Top with a final layer of tortillas, pour the remaining enchilada sauce over everything, and scatter the remaining cheddar cheese on top.
Cover and cook on low until the layers are hot through and the cheese is melted, about 3 hours — resist peeking, since every lid-lift adds cook time in a slow cooker.
Let it rest uncovered for 10 minutes so it sets up enough to scoop, then scatter the cilantro over the top before serving.
In a bowl, mix the shredded chicken with 1 cup of the cheddar cheese, the onion, cumin, salt, and 1/2 cup of the enchilada sauce.
Warm a thin layer of enchilada sauce in a large deep skillet over medium heat.
Spoon the chicken filling down the center of each tortilla, roll snugly, and nestle them seam-side down in a single snug layer in the skillet.
Pour the remaining enchilada sauce over the rolled tortillas, making sure the ends are covered so they don't dry out.

Scatter the remaining cheddar cheese over the top, cover the skillet, and simmer over low heat until the sauce is bubbling and the cheese is melted, about 12 minutes — the lid does the job the oven would, trapping heat so the cheese melts without turning on the oven.
Slide a spatula underneath to check the bottoms aren't sticking; if they are, add a small splash of water around the edges.
Let it rest off the heat for 5 minutes, then scatter the cilantro over the top before serving.
Pat the chicken thighs dry and season both sides with the paprika, salt, and pepper.

Set the pressure cooker to saute, heat the olive oil, and sear the chicken skin-side down until golden, about 5 minutes — it won't fully crisp later under pressure, but this step builds the flavor base. Remove to a plate.
Add the onion to the pot and cook in the rendered fat, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add the rice and stir for about a minute so each grain gets coated.
Pour in the chicken broth and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom — this deglazing step matters here, since stuck bits can trigger a burn warning once the pot is sealed.
Nestle the chicken thighs skin-side up on top of the rice without stirring them in — this keeps the rice from clumping under pressure.
Lock the lid, seal the valve, and cook on high pressure for 10 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then quick-release whatever remains.
Fluff the rice, scatter the parsley over the top, and serve.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the elbow macaroni until just barely tender, about 6 minutes — slightly shy of done, since it will sit in the warm cheese sauce a while longer. Drain.
Melt the butter in the same pot over medium heat, then whisk in the flour and cook, stirring, for 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the milk and cook, whisking, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon, about 6 minutes.
Remove from the heat, stir in 2 cups of the cheddar cheese, and season with salt and pepper until smooth.
Add the drained macaroni to the cheese sauce, toss to coat, then pour everything into the slow cooker.

Scatter the remaining cheddar cheese over the top, cover, and cook on low until hot through and the cheese has melted into the sauce, about 1.5 hours — the low, steady heat keeps the sauce silky without breaking it the way a hot oven can.

Meanwhile, toast the breadcrumbs in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring, until golden, about 3 minutes — since the slow cooker won't brown anything, this stovetop toast gives the crunch the baked version gets from the oven.
Scatter the toasted breadcrumbs over the mac and cheese just before serving so they stay crisp.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the elbow macaroni until just tender, about 8 minutes. Drain and set aside.
In the same pot, melt the butter over medium heat, then whisk in the flour and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Slowly pour in the milk while whisking, and cook until the sauce thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon, about 6 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in 2 cups of the cheddar cheese, seasoning with salt and pepper until smooth.
Add the cooked macaroni back to the sauce and stir until every piece is coated and heated through, about 2 minutes.
Stir in the remaining cheddar cheese a handful at a time, off the heat, until melted into the sauce — this stands in for the baked topping, since there's no oven here to melt it on top.
Meanwhile, toast the breadcrumbs in a separate dry skillet over medium heat, stirring often, until golden, about 3 minutes.
Scatter the toasted breadcrumbs over each bowl just before serving for the crunch the baked version gets from the oven.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the ziti until just barely tender, about 8 minutes — it will keep cooking in the sauce, so slightly firm is right. Drain.
In a bowl, stir together the ricotta cheese, egg, parmesan, basil, and a pinch of salt and pepper until smooth.
Add the drained ziti and half the marinara sauce to the ricotta mixture and toss to coat.
Spread a thin layer of the remaining marinara sauce in the bottom of the slow cooker.
Pour in the pasta mixture, top with the remaining marinara sauce, then scatter the mozzarella evenly over the top.

Cover and cook on low until the sauce is bubbling at the edges and the mozzarella is fully melted, about 2.5 hours — a slow cooker's gentle heat won't brown the cheese like an oven does, so expect melted and glossy rather than golden spots.
Let the dish rest with the lid off for 15 minutes before serving so it sets up enough to scoop cleanly.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the ziti until just barely tender, about 8 minutes. Drain.
Meanwhile, stir together the ricotta cheese, egg, parmesan, basil, and a pinch of salt and pepper in a bowl until smooth.

Warm half the marinara sauce in a large deep skillet over medium heat, then stir in the ricotta mixture until it forms a smooth, creamy sauce — keep the heat gentle so the egg cooks through slowly instead of curdling.
Add the drained ziti to the skillet and toss until coated, then pour the remaining marinara sauce over the top.

Scatter the mozzarella evenly over the top, cover the skillet, and cook over low heat until the cheese is fully melted and the sauce bubbles gently at the edges, about 10 minutes — the lid traps heat the way an oven would, just on the stovetop.
Uncover and let it sit for 5 minutes off the heat so the sauce sets up slightly, then serve straight from the skillet.
Warm the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion and carrot, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.

Add the ground beef, breaking it into small crumbles with a spoon, and cook until no pink remains, about 7 minutes, then transfer everything to the slow cooker — browning is the one step the slow cooker can't do on its own, so it still starts on the stove.
Stir the tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, and dried oregano into the beef mixture in the slow cooker, and season with salt and pepper.

Cover and cook on low until deeply flavorful and slightly thickened, about 6 hours (or on high for about 3 hours) — the long, slow simmer does more for a bolognese than a rushed 20 minutes ever could.
About 15 minutes before serving, bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until just tender, about 10 minutes, then drain.
Divide the spaghetti among bowls, spoon the sauce over the top, and finish with grated parmesan.
Set the pressure cooker to saute, warm the olive oil, and cook the onion and carrot, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add the ground beef, breaking it into crumbles, and cook until no pink remains, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute so it darkens slightly and loses its raw edge.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and oregano, season with salt and pepper, and scrape up any browned bits — this liquid is what keeps the pot from flagging a burn warning once it's sealed.
Lock the lid, seal the valve, and cook on high pressure for 10 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then quick-release the rest — the sauce needs this rest so it stops simmering hard enough to splatter when the lid comes off.
Meanwhile, bring a separate pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until tender, about 10 minutes, then drain.
Divide the spaghetti among bowls, spoon the sauce over the top, and finish with grated parmesan.
Brown the ground beef in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks, about 7 minutes, then drain any excess fat.
Add the onion and bell pepper to the skillet and cook until just starting to soften, about 3 minutes — they'll finish turning tender in the slow cooker.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder, and cumin and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Transfer the beef mixture to the slow cooker along with the diced tomatoes, kidney beans, and only half the beef broth — a slow cooker doesn't let liquid cook off the way a simmering pot does, so starting with less keeps the chili thick instead of soupy. Season with salt and pepper.
Cover and cook on low until deeply flavorful and thickened, about 7 hours (or on high for about 4 hours), stirring in the remaining broth only if it looks thicker than you'd like.
Taste and adjust the seasoning before ladling into bowls.
Set the pressure cooker to saute and brown the ground beef, breaking it up as it cooks, about 6 minutes, then drain any excess fat.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook until starting to soften, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder, and cumin and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the diced tomatoes, kidney beans, beef broth, salt, and pepper, and scrape up any browned bits — this matters here so the pot doesn't trigger a burn warning under pressure.
Lock the lid, seal the valve, and cook on high pressure for 15 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then quick-release whatever remains.
Stir well, taste, and adjust the seasoning — the chili will thicken slightly more as it sits, so don't worry if it looks a touch thin straight out of the pot.
In a small bowl, soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for a couple of minutes until softened.
In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, soaked breadcrumbs, egg, onion, 2 tablespoons of the ketchup, the worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper. Mix gently with your hands until just combined.

Shape the mixture into a compact loaf slightly narrower than your air fryer basket so air can circulate all the way around it — this is what crisps the outside, which the oven-baked version never gets.
Preheat the air fryer to 350 degrees.
Place the loaf in the basket and cook for 25 minutes.
Stir the remaining ketchup with the brown sugar and brush it over the top of the loaf.

Continue cooking until a thermometer inserted in the center reads 160 degrees, about 15 more minutes — check a few minutes early, since a smaller loaf cooks faster in an air fryer than a full-size one does in the oven.
Let the meatloaf rest for 10 minutes before slicing so the juices settle.
In a small bowl, soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for a couple of minutes until softened.
In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, soaked breadcrumbs, egg, onion, 2 tablespoons of the ketchup, the worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper. Mix gently with your hands until just combined.

Shape the mixture into a loaf that fits your slow cooker and set it on a foil sling or a couple of crumpled foil balls in the bottom — this lifts the loaf out of its own drippings so it doesn't sit in liquid all afternoon.
Stir the remaining ketchup with the brown sugar and spread it evenly over the top of the loaf.

Cover and cook on low until a thermometer inserted in the center reads 160 degrees, about 4 hours (or on high for about 2.5 hours) — since the slow cooker never gets hot enough to caramelize the glaze, expect it glossy and set rather than deeply browned.
Carefully lift the loaf out using the foil sling and let it rest for 10 minutes before slicing so it holds together.

Heat the grill to medium-high heat and set a cast-iron skillet directly on the grates to preheat — loose ground beef would fall through the grates on its own, so the skillet lets it pick up real grill heat and a hint of smoke.
Add the ground beef to the hot skillet and cook, breaking it into small pieces with a spatula, until browned, about 6 minutes, keeping the grill lid down between stirs to trap the smoky heat.
Drain any excess fat, then stir in the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, salt, and water.
Close the lid and simmer until the water mostly evaporates and the beef looks glossy and coated, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wrap the taco shells in foil and warm them on the cooler side of the grill for a couple of minutes.
Spoon the beef into the warm taco shells.
Top with lettuce, tomato, and cheddar cheese, and serve right away while the shells are crisp.
Divide the ground beef into 4 equal portions and shape into patties slightly wider than the buns — they shrink as they cook.
Press a shallow dimple in the center of each patty with your thumb and season both sides generously with salt and pepper.
Preheat the air fryer to 370 degrees.
Place the patties in a single layer in the basket, leaving space between them for air to circulate, and cook for 7 minutes.
Flip the patties, lay a slice of cheddar cheese on each, and cook until the cheese melts and a thermometer reads 160 degrees for medium, about 4 more minutes.
During the last minute, tuck the burger buns cut-side up into the basket alongside the patties to warm and lightly crisp.
Build each burger with lettuce, tomato, onion, and ketchup, then set the patty on top and close the bun.
Divide the ground beef into 4 equal, loose balls rather than flat patties — the griddle is what flattens them.
Heat the griddle over medium-high to high heat until a drop of water skitters and evaporates in a couple seconds.

Place the beef balls on the hot griddle, season with salt and pepper, and immediately press each one flat and thin with a sturdy spatula — this hard sear is what makes a griddle burger different from a skillet one, building a deep crust in under a minute.
Cook until deeply browned and lacy at the edges, about 2 minutes, then flip.
Lay a slice of cheddar cheese on each patty and cook until melted and the center reaches 160 degrees for medium, about 2 more minutes.
Toast the burger buns cut-side down on the griddle alongside the patties until golden, about 1 minute.
Build each burger with lettuce, tomato, onion, and ketchup, then set the patty on top and close the bun.
Divide the ground beef into 4 equal portions and shape into patties slightly wider than the buns — they shrink as they cook.
Press a shallow dimple in the center of each patty with your thumb and season both sides generously with salt and pepper.
Preheat the grill to medium-high heat and lightly oil the grates so the patties release cleanly.
Grill the patties with the lid closed until deeply marked and browned, about 4 minutes per side for medium.
Lay a slice of cheddar cheese on each patty, close the lid, and let it melt in the trapped heat, about 1 minute.
Set the burger buns cut-side down over direct heat for the last minute until lightly toasted and grill-marked.
Build each burger with lettuce, tomato, onion, and ketchup, then set the patty on top and close the bun.
Preheat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with foil for easy cleanup.
Divide the ground beef into 4 equal portions and shape into patties slightly wider than the buns — they shrink as they cook.
Season both sides generously with salt and pepper and arrange the patties on the sheet pan with space between them.
Bake until browned and cooked through, flipping once, about 12 minutes total.
Lay a slice of cheddar cheese on each patty for the last 2 minutes so it melts fully.
Tuck the burger buns cut-side up onto an empty corner of the pan for the final 2 minutes to warm and lightly toast.
Build each burger with lettuce, tomato, onion, and ketchup, then set the patty on top and close the bun.
Toss the beef cubes with the flour, salt, and pepper until lightly coated.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches, about 3 minutes per side — the slow cooker will make it tender, but only a hot pan builds this deep a flavor.
Add the onion and garlic to the same skillet and cook until the onion softens, about 4 minutes, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.

Transfer the beef and onion mixture to the slow cooker with the tomato paste, bay leaves, potatoes, and carrots. Pour in only half the broth — a slow cooker traps moisture instead of cooking it off, so extra liquid just makes a thin stew.

Cover and cook on low for about 6 hours 40 minutes, then remove the lid for the final 20 minutes and mash a few potato chunks against the side of the crock to thicken the broth naturally — the beef and vegetables should be fork-tender by the end.
Discard the bay leaves, taste and adjust the seasoning, and ladle into bowls while hot.
Toss the beef cubes with the flour, salt, and pepper until coated.
Select the sauté function on the pressure cooker, heat the olive oil, and brown the beef in batches, about 3 minutes per side — a few extra minutes here builds flavor the pressure alone can't.
Add the onion and garlic and cook, still on sauté, until the onion softens, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return the beef to the pot, pour in the broth, add the bay leaves, and nestle the potatoes and carrots on top in large chunks so they don't turn to mush.
Lock the lid and pressure cook on high for 35 minutes — the flour coating helps the broth thicken as it cooks.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then carefully turn the valve to release the rest — beef stays tender when it isn't shocked by a fast release.
Discard the bay leaves, stir well, taste and adjust the seasoning, and ladle into bowls.

Season the sliced beef sirloin with salt and pepper. Melt 1 tablespoon of the butter in a skillet over high heat and sear the beef in batches until just browned, about 1 minute per side, then transfer it straight to the slow cooker.
Melt the remaining butter in the same skillet over medium heat, add the onion and mushrooms, and cook until golden, about 7 minutes.

Stir in the garlic and flour, cook for 1 minute, then scrape the mixture and the beef broth into the slow cooker with the beef — slow cookers don't evaporate liquid the way a stovetop does, so every bit of that broth matters.
Cover and cook on low until the beef is fork-tender and the sauce has thickened slightly, about 4 hours.
Near the end of cooking, bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the egg noodles until tender, then drain.
Turn off the slow cooker and stir in the sour cream and dijon mustard until smooth — the gentler residual heat keeps the sauce from curdling the way direct stovetop heat can.
Spoon the stroganoff over the egg noodles and serve immediately.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, melt 1 tablespoon of the butter, season the beef sirloin with salt and pepper, and sear in batches until just browned, about 1 minute per side. Remove to a plate.
Melt the remaining butter in the pot, add the onion and mushrooms, and sauté until golden, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and flour and cook for 1 minute, then pour in the beef broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return the beef and any juices to the pot, lock the lid, and cook at high pressure for 8 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes before opening the valve — a natural release keeps the beef tender instead of tightening it up.
While the pot is releasing, bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the egg noodles until tender, then drain.
Stir the sour cream and dijon mustard into the pot until smooth.
Spoon the stroganoff over the egg noodles and serve immediately.
In a skillet over medium-high heat, brown the ground beef, breaking it into crumbles, about 7 minutes, then drain excess fat.
Add the onion and carrots to the skillet and cook until softened, about 5 minutes, then transfer everything to the slow cooker.
Stir the tomato paste, worcestershire sauce, and half the beef broth into the slow cooker — slow cookers don't lose liquid to evaporation, so less broth here keeps the filling from turning soupy.
Cover and cook on low until the vegetables are tender and the filling bubbles gently at the edges, about 5 hours.
Near the end of cooking, put the potatoes in a pot of salted water, bring to a boil, and cook until tender when pierced with a fork, about 15 minutes.
Drain the potatoes and mash them with the butter and milk until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir the frozen peas into the filling, then spoon the mashed potato over the top in an even layer.
Cover and cook on high for 15 more minutes just to heat the potatoes through — the top won't turn golden under a lid the way it does in an oven, but it stays warm and creamy.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the lasagna noodles until just tender, about 9 minutes, then drain and lay flat so they don't stick.
In a skillet over medium-high heat, brown the ground beef with the onion, breaking the meat into small pieces, about 7 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, crushed tomatoes, and dried basil, season with salt and pepper, and simmer for 5 minutes.
In a bowl, stir together the ricotta cheese, egg, and a pinch of salt and pepper until smooth.

Spread a thin layer of meat sauce in the bottom of the slow cooker insert, then layer noodles (breaking them to fit the round shape), ricotta mixture, meat sauce, and mozzarella. Repeat the layers, ending with sauce and mozzarella on top.
Sprinkle the parmesan over the top, cover, and cook on low until the noodles are tender and the cheese is melted, about 4 hours — resist lifting the lid, since every peek adds cooking time.
Turn off the slow cooker and let the lasagna rest with the lid ajar for 15 minutes so the layers set before slicing.
Cook the ground beef in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it into small pieces, until browned, about 6 minutes, then drain excess fat.
Add the onion and bell pepper to the skillet and cook until just softened, about 3 minutes.
Transfer the beef mixture to the slow cooker and stir in the ketchup, brown sugar, worcestershire sauce, and tomato paste, and season with salt and pepper.
Cover and cook on low until thick and glossy, about 3 hours, stirring once partway through.
Toast the burger buns lightly if you like, then pile the beef mixture generously onto the bottom halves and close with the tops.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté and brown the ground beef, breaking it into small pieces, about 6 minutes, then drain excess fat.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the ketchup, brown sugar, worcestershire sauce, and tomato paste, and season with salt and pepper.
Cancel sauté, lock the lid, and cook at high pressure for 5 minutes.
Quick release the pressure right away — there's no large cut of meat here to protect, so there's no reason to wait.
Switch back to sauté and simmer uncovered for a few minutes if the mixture looks thin, about 3 minutes, until thick and glossy.
Toast the burger buns lightly if you like, then pile the beef mixture generously onto the bottom halves and close with the tops.
In a large bowl, mix the ground beef, breadcrumbs, parmesan, egg, half the garlic, salt, and pepper until just combined.
Roll the mixture into golf ball-sized meatballs, about 16 total.
