Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and brown the meatballs on all sides, about 6 minutes — they just need color, not to cook through.

Transfer the meatballs to the slow cooker. Add the remaining garlic to the skillet, stir for 30 seconds, then pour in the crushed tomatoes and dried basil, season with salt and pepper, and pour the sauce over the meatballs.
Cover and cook on low until the meatballs are cooked through and tender, about 4 hours.
Serve the meatballs and sauce hot, spooning extra sauce over the top.
In a large bowl, mix the ground beef, breadcrumbs, parmesan, egg, half the garlic, salt, and pepper until just combined.
Roll the mixture into golf ball-sized meatballs, about 16 total.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, heat the olive oil, and brown the meatballs on all sides in batches, about 6 minutes.
Remove the meatballs, add the remaining garlic, and stir for 30 seconds, then pour in the crushed tomatoes and dried basil, season with salt and pepper, and scrape up any browned bits.
Nestle the meatballs back into the sauce, lock the lid, and cook at high pressure for 8 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes before opening — a natural release keeps the meatballs from bouncing around and breaking apart.
Serve the meatballs and sauce hot, spooning extra sauce over the top.
Preheat the griddle to medium-high heat and lightly oil the surface.
Spread the onion and bell pepper on the griddle and cook, stirring, until soft and lightly browned, about 8 minutes, then push them to a cooler zone.
Add the remaining vegetable oil to a hotter section of the griddle, lay the sliced ribeye in a thin layer, and season with salt and pepper.
Chop the steak into smaller pieces with a spatula as it sears, mixing in the peppers and onions, until no pink remains, about 4 minutes.
Divide the mixture into 4 mounds, lay 2 slices of provolone cheese over each, and cover with a melting dome until the cheese melts, about 2 minutes.
Meanwhile, toast the hoagie rolls cut-side down on an open section of the griddle until golden, about 1 minute.
Scoop each cheesy mound into a hoagie roll and serve right away.
Preheat the grill to medium-high heat and set a large cast iron skillet directly on the grates to heat, about 5 minutes — the skillet keeps the thin-sliced meat and vegetables from falling through.
Add half the vegetable oil to the skillet, then the onion and bell pepper, and cook with the lid closed until soft and lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Move the vegetables to a plate, add the remaining oil, and lay the sliced ribeye in a thin layer, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Chop the steak into smaller pieces with a spatula as it browns, until no pink remains, about 4 minutes.
Return the onion and bell pepper to the skillet and mix with the steak.
Divide into 4 mounds, top each with 2 slices of provolone cheese, close the grill lid, and let the cheese melt in the trapped heat, about 2 minutes.
Split the hoagie rolls and warm them cut-side down directly on the grill grates for the last minute.
Scoop the cheesy steak into the rolls and serve right away.
Preheat the griddle to medium-high heat.
Crumble the ground beef onto the griddle and cook, chopping it into small pieces with a spatula, until browned, about 6 minutes, then scrape off excess grease.
Push the beef aside, add the garlic and ginger to a hotter spot, and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds, then mix everything together.
Drizzle the soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, and red pepper flakes over the beef and toss to coat, letting the sauce bubble and cling to the meat, about 3 minutes.
Spoon the beef over bowls of warm rice.
Scatter the green onion and sesame seeds over the top before serving.
Preheat the grill to medium-high heat and set a large cast iron skillet on the grates to heat, about 5 minutes — ground beef needs a solid surface, since it would fall straight through the grates.
Crumble the ground beef into the skillet and cook with the lid closed, breaking it into small pieces, until browned, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add the soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, and red pepper flakes, close the lid, and let it bubble until it clings to the meat, about 3 minutes.
Spoon the beef over bowls of warm rice.
Scatter the green onion and sesame seeds over the top before serving.
Preheat the oven to 450°F.
Crumble the ground beef onto a rimmed sheet pan in an even layer.
Roast until browned, breaking it up with a spatula halfway through, about 10 minutes.
Stir the garlic, ginger, soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, and red pepper flakes right into the beef on the pan, spreading it back into a thin layer.
Return to the oven and roast until the sauce is bubbling and slightly sticky, about 5 minutes.
Spoon the beef over bowls of warm rice.
Scatter the green onion and sesame seeds over the top before serving.
Pat the roast dry and season it all over generously with salt and pepper.

Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and sear the roast on all sides until deeply browned, about 10 minutes total — the slow cooker won't brown anything later, so this step is where the flavor gets built.
Add the onion to the skillet and cook until it softens and picks up the browned bits, about 4 minutes. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook 1 minute more.

Transfer the onion mixture to the slow cooker, set the roast on top, and tuck the carrots and potatoes in around it along with the bay leaves and thyme. Pour in only half the broth — a slow cooker doesn't lose liquid to evaporation the way an oven does, so more broth just dilutes the sauce.
Cover and cook on low until the roast shreds easily with a fork and the vegetables are tender, about 8 hours.
Lift the roast onto a cutting board, discard the bay leaves, and let it rest for 10 minutes before slicing or shredding.
Serve the sliced roast with the vegetables and spoon the cooking juices over the top.
Pat the roast dry and season it all over generously with salt and pepper.
Select the sauté function on the pressure cooker, heat the olive oil, and sear the roast on all sides until deeply browned, about 8 minutes total.
Remove the roast, add the onion, and cook until it softens and picks up the browned bits, about 3 minutes. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook 1 minute more.
Pour in the broth to deglaze, scraping up any browned bits, then return the roast to the pot along with the bay leaves and thyme.
Lock the lid and pressure cook on high for 60 minutes — the same roast that takes 3 hours in the oven turns tender in a fraction of the time under pressure.
Let the pressure release naturally for 15 minutes, then carefully release any remaining pressure.
Nestle the carrots and potatoes around the roast, lock the lid, and pressure cook on high for 8 minutes more, then quick-release the valve.
Lift the roast onto a cutting board, discard the bay leaves, and let it rest for 10 minutes before slicing or shredding.
Serve the sliced roast with the vegetables and spoon the cooking juices over the top.
Pat the chuck roast dry and season all over generously with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and sear the roast on all sides until deeply browned, about 10 minutes total. Set the roast aside.
Add the onion to the pot and cook until it starts to soften and picks up the browned bits, about 4 minutes. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the beef broth, add the bay leaves and thyme, and return the roast to the pot.

Bring to a gentle simmer, then lower the heat until the liquid barely bubbles, cover, and cook on the stovetop until the roast starts to turn tender, about 2 hours — a hard boil on the stove toughens the meat, so keep it low and slow.
Add the carrots and potatoes around the roast, cover, and continue simmering until the meat shreds easily with a fork and the vegetables are tender, about 50 minutes.
Lift the roast onto a cutting board, discard the bay leaves, and let it rest for 10 minutes before slicing or shredding.
Serve the sliced roast with the vegetables and spoon the pan juices over the top.
Pat the pork chops dry and season both sides generously with salt and pepper.
Preheat the air fryer to 380°F, about 3 minutes.
Lightly coat the air fryer basket, arrange the pork chops in a single layer without touching, and air fry until golden and cooked through, flipping halfway, about 12 minutes.
While the chops cook, melt the butter in a small skillet over medium heat, add the onion, and cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add the apples and dried thyme and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and golden at the edges, about 5 minutes.
Pour in the chicken broth, scrape up any browned bits, and simmer until slightly thickened, about 3 minutes.
Check the chops for doneness — they're ready at 145°F on an instant read thermometer; give them another minute or two in the basket if needed.
Serve the pork chops topped with the apples and pan sauce.
Pat the pork chops dry and season both sides generously with salt and pepper.
Preheat the grill to medium-high heat, about 10 minutes.
Grill the chops directly over the heat until nicely marked and cooked through, about 5 minutes per side.
Move the chops to a platter to rest while you make the topping.
Melt the butter in a small skillet over medium heat, add the onion, and cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add the apples and dried thyme and cook until softened and golden at the edges, about 5 minutes.
Pour in the chicken broth, scrape up any browned bits, and simmer until slightly thickened, about 3 minutes.
Serve the grilled pork chops topped with the apples and pan sauce.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Pat the pork chops dry, season with salt and pepper, and arrange on a sheet pan.
Melt the butter and toss it with the onion, apples, and dried thyme in a bowl, then scatter the mixture around the chops on the pan.
Drizzle the chicken broth over the apples and onion.
Roast until the chops are cooked through and the apples are tender and golden at the edges, about 18 minutes, stirring the apples once halfway through.
Serve the pork chops topped with the roasted apples and pan juices.
In a small bowl, mix the brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper to make a dry rub.
Rub the mixture all over the pork shoulder, pressing it into the surface.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté and sear the pork shoulder on all sides until browned, about 8 minutes.
Remove the pork, add the onion to the pot, and stir for 1 minute to loosen the browned bits.
Pour in the chicken broth and apple cider vinegar and return the pork to the pot.
Lock the lid and cook at high pressure for 60 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 15 minutes before opening — releasing it early can shock the meat and make it harder to shred.
Lift the pork onto a cutting board and shred it with two forks, discarding any large pieces of fat.
Return the shredded pork to the pot and toss with enough of the cooking liquid to keep it moist.
Pile the pulled pork onto burger buns and serve warm.

Rub the mixture all over the pork shoulder, pressing it into the surface.
Heat a large pot over medium-high heat and sear the pork shoulder on all sides until browned, about 8 minutes.

Pour in the chicken broth and apple cider vinegar and cover the pot.

Bring to a boil, then reduce to a bare simmer and cook, covered, until the pork shreds easily with a fork, about 3 hours, turning it once partway through and checking that the liquid hasn't dried out.

Cover and cook on low until the pork shreds easily with a fork, about 7 hours.
Shred the pork right in the slow cooker with two forks, then switch to high, uncover, and simmer for 15 minutes to concentrate the juices and cook off any extra liquid.
Spread the shredded pork on a baking sheet and broil until the edges turn crisp and golden, about 5 minutes, watching closely so it doesn't burn.
Pile the crispy pork into warm corn tortillas and top with the diced onion and cilantro.
Season the pork chunks generously with salt and pepper.
Select the sauté function on the pressure cooker and toast the cumin and dried oregano for about 30 seconds, just until fragrant — it wakes the spices up before the liquid goes in.
Add the garlic, orange juice, lime juice, and chicken broth, scraping up anything stuck to the bottom of the pot.
Add the pork chunks and nestle them into the liquid.
Lock the lid and pressure cook on high for 45 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 15 minutes — carnitas fall apart best when they aren't rushed off the heat — then release any remaining pressure.
Shred the pork right in the pot with two forks, then select sauté and simmer, uncovered, for 8 minutes to boil off most of the liquid.
Spread the shredded pork on a baking sheet and broil until the edges turn crisp and golden, about 5 minutes, watching closely so it doesn't burn.
Pile the crispy pork into warm corn tortillas and top with the diced onion and cilantro.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and brown the sausage links on all sides, about 6 minutes. Slice into thick coins once cool enough to handle.
Add the onion to the skillet and cook until softened, about 4 minutes, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.

Transfer the sausage and onion mixture to the slow cooker. Stir in the diced tomatoes, cannellini beans, half the chicken broth, and dried rosemary, and season with salt and pepper — slow cookers don't evaporate, so a splash less broth keeps the casserole from turning watery.
Cover and cook on low until bubbling and the flavors have melded, about 4 hours.
Serve hot straight from the slow cooker.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, heat the olive oil, and brown the sausage links on all sides, about 6 minutes. Slice into thick coins once cool enough to handle.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 4 minutes, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, cannellini beans, chicken broth, and dried rosemary, season with salt and pepper, and nestle the sliced sausage back in.
Lock the lid and cook at high pressure for 5 minutes.
Quick release the pressure — the beans are already soft from the can, so there's no reason to wait.
Switch back to sauté and simmer uncovered for a few minutes if you'd like it thicker, about 3 minutes.
Serve hot straight from the pot.
Toss the pork cubes with the beaten egg, then coat evenly in half the cornstarch, shaking off the excess.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F, about 3 minutes.
Lightly coat the air fryer basket and arrange the pork in a single layer, air frying until golden and cooked through, shaking the basket halfway, about 10 minutes.

While the pork cooks, heat a splash of the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat, add the bell pepper, and cook until just tender, about 3 minutes — the air fryer does the frying now, so the peppers only need a little oil.
In a small bowl, whisk together the ketchup, rice vinegar, brown sugar, soy sauce, and the remaining cornstarch dissolved in 3 tablespoons of water.
Pour the sauce into the skillet with the bell pepper and simmer until thickened and glossy, about 2 minutes.
Add the pineapple and the air-fried pork to the skillet and toss until everything is coated and warmed through, about 2 minutes.
Serve immediately over cooked rice.
Preheat the griddle to medium-high heat and add 1 tablespoon of the vegetable oil to one section.
Add the pork to the hot oil and cook, spreading it out, until browned and cooked through, about 4 minutes, then push it to a cooler zone.
Pour the beaten eggs onto an open section of the griddle and scramble with a spatula until just set, about 1 minute, then push them over with the pork.
Add the remaining oil, then the onion, and cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the frozen peas and carrots and the garlic and cook until heated through, about 2 minutes.
Spread the cold rice across the hottest part of the griddle, breaking up any clumps with the spatula, and stir-fry until it starts to crisp in spots, about 4 minutes.
Push everything together, return the pork and eggs, drizzle with the soy sauce and sesame oil, and toss until evenly combined and heated through, about 2 minutes.
Sprinkle the green onion over the top and serve hot.
Put the potatoes in a large pot of salted water, bring to a boil, and cook until tender, about 15 minutes.
Preheat the air fryer to 380°F, about 3 minutes.
Arrange the sausages in the air fryer basket in a single layer and air fry, turning halfway, until browned and cooked through, about 14 minutes.

Drain the potatoes and mash with the remaining butter and the milk until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Return the sausages to the gravy to warm through, about 1 minute.
Serve the sausages and onion gravy over a mound of mashed potato.
Pat the pork tenderloin dry and season all over with salt and pepper.
Rub the tenderloin with the olive oil, curl the thin tail end underneath itself so it cooks at an even thickness, and set it in the air fryer basket.
Air fry at 380°F until lightly browned on the outside, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk the honey, dijon mustard, garlic, and apple cider vinegar together in a small bowl to make the glaze.
Brush the tenderloin with half the glaze, flip it, and air fry 5 more minutes — in the tight space of a basket the glaze can catch fast, so keep an eye on it.
Brush with the remaining glaze and continue air frying until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 145°F, about 6 to 8 minutes more.
Move the tenderloin to a cutting board and let it rest 5 minutes before slicing so the juices redistribute.
Pat the pork tenderloin dry and season all over with salt and pepper.
Rub it all over with the olive oil, then preheat the grill to medium-high and set up two zones — direct heat on one side, a cooler indirect area on the other.
Sear the tenderloin directly over the hot side, turning every couple of minutes, until browned on all sides, about 8 minutes total.
While it sears, whisk the honey, dijon mustard, garlic, and apple cider vinegar together in a small bowl to make the glaze.
Move the tenderloin to the cooler side of the grill, brush with half the glaze, and close the lid.

Grill with the lid closed, brushing with the remaining glaze once or twice, until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 145°F, about 12 to 15 minutes — indirect heat lets the glaze caramelize without scorching.
Transfer to a cutting board, tent loosely with foil, and rest 5 minutes before slicing.
Heat the oven to 425°F and set a sheet pan nearby.
Pat the pork tenderloin dry, season all over with salt and pepper, and rub with the olive oil.
Set the tenderloin on the sheet pan and roast for 15 minutes to start building color, since a sheet pan won't sear the meat the way a hot skillet does.
Meanwhile, whisk the honey, dijon mustard, garlic, and apple cider vinegar together in a small bowl to make the glaze.
Brush the tenderloin with half the glaze and return the sheet pan to the oven for 8 minutes.
Brush with the remaining glaze and roast until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 145°F, about 5 to 7 minutes more.
Let the tenderloin rest on the sheet pan for 5 minutes before slicing, spooning any pan juices back over the top.
Pat the salmon fillets dry and season with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter and stir in the lemon juice, garlic, and dried dill.
Preheat the air fryer to 380°F for a few minutes — starting hot gives the fillets a bit of color they'd otherwise miss without a broiler.
Brush the salmon all over with the butter mixture and set the fillets skin-side down in the air fryer basket, leaving space between them.
Lay the lemon slices over the top of the fillets.
Air fry until the salmon flakes easily and looks opaque in the center, about 8 to 10 minutes — no need to flip.
Let the fillets rest a couple of minutes, then drizzle with any butter mixture left in the bowl before serving.
Pat the salmon fillets dry and season with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter and stir in the lemon juice, garlic, and dried dill.
Preheat the grill to medium and oil the grates well — skinless fillets stick easily, so don't skip this.
Lay the lemon slices in a row on the grates and set the salmon on top of them skin-side down; the lemon keeps the delicate fish from falling through or sticking.
Brush the fillets with the butter mixture, close the lid, and grill until the salmon flakes easily and is opaque throughout, about 8 to 10 minutes — resist flipping it.
Lift the fillets off, lemon slices and all, using a wide spatula.
Drizzle with any remaining butter mixture before serving.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the linguine until just short of tender, about 1 minute less than the package says. Scoop out a cup of the pasta water before draining.
Toss the shrimp with the olive oil, salt, and pepper, then thread them onto skewers.
Preheat the grill to medium-high and oil the grates.
Grill the shrimp skewers until pink, curled, and lightly charred, about 2 minutes per side.
Meanwhile, melt half the butter in a small skillet over medium heat, add the garlic and red pepper flakes, and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Pour in the white wine and let it bubble for a minute to cook off the sharp smell.
Stir in the remaining butter and the lemon juice until the sauce looks glossy.
Slide the shrimp off the skewers into the skillet, add the drained linguine, and toss well, splashing in reserved pasta water a little at a time until the sauce coats the noodles.
Scatter the parsley over the top and serve right away while the sauce is still glossy.
Toss the cabbage with the mayonnaise and half the lime juice in a bowl, season with salt, and set aside so it softens while you cook the fish.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F.
Pat the fish dry and rub both sides with the olive oil, chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Set the fish in the air fryer basket in a single layer and air fry until it flakes easily and the edges are golden, about 8 minutes, flipping halfway.
Move the fish to a plate and break it into large flaky chunks with a fork.
Stack the tortillas, wrap loosely in foil, and warm them in the air fryer for a couple of minutes while the fish rests.
Fill each tortilla with fish and a spoonful of the cabbage slaw.
Top with cilantro and a squeeze of the remaining lime juice before serving.
Toss the cabbage with the mayonnaise and half the lime juice in a bowl, season with salt, and set aside so it softens while you cook the fish.
Preheat the grill to medium-high and oil the grates well — white fish is delicate and sticks fast.
Pat the fish dry and rub both sides with the olive oil, chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Grill the fish until it releases easily and flakes apart, with good char marks, about 3 to 4 minutes per side.
Move the fish to a plate and break it into large flaky chunks with a fork.
Warm the tortillas directly on the grill grates, about 15 to 20 seconds per side, until soft and lightly charred.
Fill each tortilla with fish and a spoonful of the cabbage slaw.
Top with cilantro and a squeeze of the remaining lime juice before serving.
Melt the butter in a small saucepan on the stovetop, whisk in the flour, and cook for 1 minute until it smells toasty, not raw.
Slowly whisk in the milk until smooth, then pour the mixture into the slow cooker.
Add the uncooked pasta, half the cheddar cheese, and salt and pepper to the slow cooker and stir to coat the pasta in the sauce.
Cover and cook on low until the pasta is tender, about 2 1/2 hours, stirring once around the halfway mark so it doesn't clump or stick to the bottom.
Stir in the tuna and frozen peas during the last 20 minutes of cooking, so they heat through without turning rubbery or falling apart.
Stir in the remaining cheddar cheese until melted.
Meanwhile, toast the breadcrumbs in a dry skillet over medium heat until golden, about 3 minutes, stirring often — this gives you a crunchy topping a slow cooker can't.
Scatter the toasted breadcrumbs over each portion just before serving so they stay crisp.
Soak the cut potatoes in a bowl of cold water for at least 15 minutes to rinse away extra starch, then drain and pat completely dry.
Toss the dried potatoes with 1 tablespoon of the vegetable oil and a pinch of salt.

Preheat the air fryer to 380°F, then air fry the potatoes in a single layer, shaking the basket every 5 minutes, until golden and crisp, about 18 to 20 minutes. Move them to a bowl and raise the temperature to 400°F.
Whisk the remaining flour, the cornstarch, the baking powder, and a pinch of salt and pepper together in a bowl for the dry coating.

Pat the fish dry, dip each piece briefly in the cold sparkling water, then press it into the dry coating until evenly covered, patting off the excess — the fizzy water helps the coating cling without needing a deep-fry batter.
Lightly brush or spray both sides of the coated fish with vegetable oil and set the pieces in the air fryer basket in a single layer.
Air fry at 400°F, flipping once halfway, until deep golden and the fish flakes easily, about 10 to 12 minutes total.
Return the potatoes to the basket for the last 2 minutes just to re-crisp and warm through.
Serve the fish and chips hot with malt vinegar on the side.
Whisk the soy sauce, honey, and cornstarch together in a small bowl until smooth and set aside.
Toss the broccoli, bell pepper, and carrot with half the vegetable oil.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F, then air fry the vegetables in the basket, shaking once, until bright and just tender-crisp, about 8 minutes. Move them to a bowl.
Toss the shrimp with the remaining vegetable oil, garlic, and ginger.
Set the shrimp in the basket in a single layer and air fry until pink and curled, about 6 minutes, shaking halfway.
Meanwhile, warm the sauce in a small saucepan on the stovetop until it thickens and turns glossy, about 1 minute — the air fryer can't reduce a sauce for you.
Toss the air-fried vegetables and shrimp with the warm sauce until everything is coated, then serve hot.
Whisk the soy sauce, honey, and cornstarch together in a small bowl until smooth and set aside.
Thread the shrimp onto skewers. Toss the broccoli, bell pepper, and carrot with half the vegetable oil and load them into a grill basket.
Preheat the grill to medium-high and oil the grates.
Grill the vegetables in the grill basket, tossing occasionally, until charred at the edges and just tender-crisp, about 7 minutes.
Brush the shrimp skewers with the remaining vegetable oil, then grill until pink, curled, and lightly charred, about 2 minutes per side.
Meanwhile, add the garlic and ginger to a small saucepan with the sauce and simmer over medium heat, stirring, until fragrant and thickened, about 2 minutes.
Slide the shrimp off the skewers, toss everything with the grilled vegetables and warm sauce, and serve hot.
Stir the tuna, mayonnaise, and celery together in a bowl, then season with salt and pepper.
Lay out the bread slices and spread the tuna mixture evenly over two of them.
Top the tuna with the cheddar cheese, then close each sandwich with the remaining bread.
Butter the outside of each sandwich on both sides.
Preheat the griddle over medium heat — its flat, wide surface heats more evenly edge to edge than a skillet, so both sandwiches toast at the same rate.
Set the sandwiches on the griddle and cook until golden and crisp on the first side, about 3 minutes.
Flip carefully and cook the second side until golden and the cheese has melted through, about 3 more minutes.
Slice in half and serve while the cheese is still warm and stretchy.
Cook the white rice according to the package directions and keep it warm.
Whisk the tamari, honey, rice vinegar, and sesame oil together in a small bowl.
Preheat the air fryer to 380°F.
Pat the salmon dry, brush with half the sauce, and set it skin-side down in the air fryer basket.
Air fry until the fish flakes easily and looks opaque in the center, about 8 minutes, brushing with a little more sauce halfway through for a sticky glaze.
Break the salmon into large chunks.
Divide the warm rice between two bowls and top with the salmon, cucumber, and avocado.
Drizzle the remaining sauce over the bowls and finish with a scatter of sesame seeds.
Cook the white rice according to the package directions and keep it warm.
Whisk the tamari, honey, rice vinegar, and sesame oil together in a small bowl.
Preheat the grill to medium-high and oil the grates well — skinless salmon sticks fast without it.
Brush the salmon with a little of the sesame oil and set it on the hot grates. Let it sit untouched until it releases easily and has good grill marks, about 4 minutes.
Flip carefully, brush with half the sauce, and grill until the fish flakes easily, about 3 to 4 minutes more.
Break the salmon into large chunks.
Divide the warm rice between two bowls and top with the salmon, cucumber, and avocado.
Drizzle the remaining sauce over the bowls and finish with a scatter of sesame seeds.
Cook the white rice according to the package directions and keep it warm.
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with foil.
Whisk the tamari, honey, rice vinegar, and sesame oil together in a small bowl.
Pat the salmon dry, set it on the sheet pan, and brush with half the sauce.
Roast until the salmon is just about opaque at the edges, about 8 minutes.
Brush with the remaining sauce and roast until it flakes easily and looks glossy, about 3 to 4 more minutes.
Break the salmon into large chunks.
Divide the warm rice between two bowls, top with the salmon, cucumber, and avocado, and finish with a scatter of sesame seeds.

Cook the bacon in a skillet on the stovetop over medium heat until crisp, about 5 minutes, then lift it out onto a paper towel, leaving the fat in the pan — a slow cooker won't crisp bacon, so this step still needs the stovetop.
Add the onion and celery to the bacon fat and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir constantly for 1 minute, then scrape everything into the slow cooker.
Stir the reserved clam juice from the cans and the bottled clam juice into the slow cooker, along with the potatoes and bay leaf.
Cover and cook on low until the potatoes are fork-tender, about 4 1/2 hours.
Stir in the heavy cream and milk during the last 20 minutes so they warm through gently — added any earlier, the dairy can break under hours of heat.
Add the chopped clams in the last 5 minutes and re-cover — clams turn rubbery fast, so they only need enough time to heat through, not to cook further.
Remove the bay leaf, season with salt and pepper, and ladle into bowls topped with the reserved crisp bacon.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, cook the bacon until crisp, about 5 minutes, then lift it out onto a paper towel, leaving the fat behind.
Add the onion and celery to the fat and cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir constantly for 1 minute, then pour in the reserved clam juice from the cans and the bottled clam juice, scraping up any browned bits.
Add the potatoes and bay leaf, lock the lid, and pressure cook on high for 5 minutes.
Quick release the pressure as soon as it's done — letting it sit would carry the potatoes past tender into mushy.
Switch back to sauté, stir in the heavy cream and milk, and warm through gently, about 3 minutes — do not let it boil hard.
Stir in the chopped clams and cook just 2 minutes on sauté — added at the very end so the pressure cycle never touches them and they stay tender.
Remove the bay leaf, season with salt and pepper, and ladle into bowls topped with the reserved crisp bacon.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet on the stovetop and cook the onion and carrots until softened, about 5 minutes — a quick sauté first builds more flavor than dropping everything in raw.
Add the garlic and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds, then scrape everything into the slow cooker.
Add the vegetable broth and diced tomatoes to the slow cooker and season with salt and pepper.
Cover and cook on low until the vegetables are tender and the flavors have melded, about 5 hours (or high for 2 1/2 hours).
Stir in the tortellini during the last 20 minutes of cooking on high — fresh tortellini turns to mush if it simmers for hours, so it only goes in near the end.
Stir in the spinach in the last 5 minutes, just until wilted.
Ladle into bowls and top with parmesan cheese before serving.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, heat the olive oil, and cook the onion and carrots until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add the garlic and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Pour in the vegetable broth and diced tomatoes, season with salt and pepper, and scrape up any browned bits.
Lock the lid and pressure cook on high for 3 minutes, then quick release — the vegetables just need to finish softening and the flavors to meld.

Switch back to sauté, stir in the tortellini, and simmer gently until tender and floating, about 4 minutes — pressure cooking fresh tortellini directly would turn it to paste, so it finishes in the open pot instead.
Stir in the spinach and cook just until wilted, about 1 minute.
Ladle into bowls and top with parmesan cheese before serving.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, melt 2 tablespoons of the butter, and add the mushrooms in a single layer. Cook without stirring too much until deeply browned, about 6 minutes, then set aside.
Add 2 more tablespoons of butter to the pot along with the onion, cooking until soft, about 4 minutes.
Add the arborio rice and stir for about a minute until the edges of the grains look slightly translucent.
Pour in the white wine and stir until it's absorbed, about 1 minute.
Add all of the vegetable broth at once — pressure cooking means you don't need to add it gradually the way you would on the stovetop. Lock the lid and pressure cook on high for 6 minutes.
Quick release the pressure as soon as it's done — letting the rice sit under natural release would carry it past creamy into mushy.
Stir the browned mushrooms, remaining butter, and parmesan cheese back in, switching to sauté for a minute or two and stirring constantly until glossy and creamy — this mimics the stovetop finish.
Season with salt and pepper and serve immediately, while it's still loose and creamy.
Heat the oven to 375°F.

Melt 2 tablespoons of the butter in an oven-safe pot over medium-high heat on the stovetop and add the mushrooms in a single layer. Cook without stirring too much until deeply browned, about 6 minutes, then set aside.
Add 2 more tablespoons of butter to the same pot along with the onion, cooking until soft, about 4 minutes.
Add the arborio rice and stir for about a minute until the edges of the grains look slightly translucent.
Pour in the white wine and stir until it's absorbed, about 1 minute.

Pour in all of the vegetable broth at once, stir once, cover the pot tightly, and transfer it to the oven — the oven's steady heat means you don't have to stand and stir constantly like you would on the stovetop.
Bake until the rice is tender with just a little bite left and the broth is mostly absorbed, about 20 minutes.

Stir the browned mushrooms, remaining butter, and parmesan cheese in vigorously for about a minute until glossy and creamy — the vigorous stirring at the end releases the rice's starch and mimics a stovetop finish.
Season with salt and pepper and serve immediately, while it's still loose and creamy.
Preheat the air fryer to 370°F.
Stir the crushed tomatoes, garlic, salt, and pepper together in a small bowl.
Brush both flatbreads lightly with olive oil on one side.
Spread the tomato mixture evenly over the oiled side of each flatbread, leaving a small border.
Arrange the mozzarella slices over the top of each flatbread.

Place one flatbread at a time in the air fryer basket — most baskets only fit one, and crowding blocks the hot air that crisps the crust — and air fry until the cheese is melted and bubbling and the edges are golden, about 6 to 8 minutes.
Repeat with the second flatbread while the first stays warm.
Scatter the basil over both, slice, and serve hot.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet on the stovetop and cook the onion until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, and curry powder, stirring until fragrant, about 1 minute, then scrape everything into the slow cooker.

Add the sweet potato, diced tomatoes, and only half the vegetable broth to the slow cooker — a slow cooker traps all its moisture instead of letting it evaporate, so the full amount would turn the curry watery.
Cover and cook on low until the sweet potato is fork-tender, about 6 1/2 hours (or high for 3 1/2 hours).
Stir in the peanut butter until fully melted into the sauce, then cover and cook 10 more minutes on high to let it meld.
Stir in the spinach, cover, and cook just until wilted, about 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve warm.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, heat the olive oil, and cook the onion until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, and curry powder, stirring until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the sweet potato, diced tomatoes, and all of the vegetable broth — under pressure nothing evaporates, so unlike a slow cooker, the full amount is fine here.
Lock the lid and pressure cook on high for 8 minutes, then quick release.
Switch back to sauté, stir in the peanut butter until melted, and simmer uncovered for 3 minutes to thicken slightly.
Stir in the spinach and cook just until wilted, about 1 minute.
Season with salt and pepper and serve warm.
Whisk the soy sauce, cornstarch, and vegetable broth together in a small bowl until smooth; set aside.
Toss the broccoli and carrots with half the vegetable oil.

Preheat the air fryer to 400°F, then air fry the broccoli and carrots, shaking the basket halfway, until bright and starting to crisp at the edges, about 8 minutes — these take longest, so they go in first.
Toss the bell pepper and snap peas with the remaining oil, add them to the basket, and air fry until all the vegetables are bright and tender-crisp, about 4 more minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger to the basket for the final minute so they turn fragrant without burning — hot circulating air scorches minced garlic fast, so it goes in last, not first.
Meanwhile, warm the sauce in a small saucepan on the stovetop until it thickens and turns glossy, about 2 minutes — the air fryer can't reduce a sauce for you.
Toss the air-fried vegetables with the warm sauce until evenly coated.
Serve right away while the edges are still crisp - the sauce softens them as they sit.
Whisk the soy sauce, cornstarch, and vegetable broth together in a small bowl until smooth and set aside.
Heat the grill to high with a grill basket set on top to preheat, and rub the basket well with a little of the vegetable oil so nothing sticks.
Toss the broccoli and carrots with a splash of vegetable oil, spread them in the hot basket, and grill with the lid down, tossing once, until they start to char at the edges, about 5 minutes.
Add the bell pepper and snap peas to the basket and keep grilling until all the vegetables are bright and lightly charred, about 4 more minutes.

Push the vegetables to one side of the basket, scatter the garlic and ginger into the cleared space, and let them sit over the heat just until fragrant, about 1 minute — watch closely, since grill heat runs hotter than a stovetop burner.
Set a small saucepan directly on the grill grate, pour in the sauce, and whisk until it thickens and turns glossy, about 2 minutes.
Pour the sauce over the grilled vegetables in the basket and toss everything together until well coated.
Serve hot, straight off the grill.
Preheat the oven to 425°F with a sheet pan inside — a hot pan means the vegetables sear on contact instead of steaming.
Whisk the soy sauce, cornstarch, and vegetable broth together in a small bowl until smooth and set aside.
Toss the broccoli and carrots with the vegetable oil, carefully spread them in a single layer on the hot sheet pan, and roast for 8 minutes.
Add the bell pepper and snap peas to the pan, toss, and roast until all the vegetables are bright and lightly browned at the edges, about 7 more minutes.
Push the vegetables to one side of the pan, scatter the garlic and ginger onto the cleared space, and return to the oven just until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Pour the sauce directly over the vegetables on the pan and toss well to coat.
Return the pan to the oven for 2 minutes, until the sauce clings to the vegetables and looks glossy and thickened.
Serve hot, straight off the pan.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion and bell peppers until softened, about 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, chili powder, and cumin, stirring until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Scrape the mixture into the slow cooker.

Stir in the diced tomatoes, black beans, kidney beans, corn, and only half the vegetable broth — a slow cooker traps moisture instead of letting it cook off, so starting lighter on liquid keeps the chili thick.
Cover and cook on low for 7 hours, or on high for 4 hours, until the vegetables are completely tender and the chili has thickened.
Season with salt and pepper, stir well, and serve hot straight from the slow cooker.
Set the pressure cooker to the sauté function, heat the olive oil, and cook the onion and bell peppers until softened, about 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, chili powder, and cumin, stirring until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, black beans, kidney beans, corn, and vegetable broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot so nothing scorches once it's sealed.
Lock the lid, set the valve to sealing, and cook on high pressure for 8 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then carefully switch the valve to venting to release any steam left.
Open the lid, season with salt and pepper, stir, and serve — the beans will have soaked up even more flavor than the stovetop version, in a fraction of the time.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft and golden at the edges, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, and curry powder, stirring until fragrant, about 1 minute — blooming the spices in oil now means they still taste bright after hours in the slow cooker.
Transfer everything to the slow cooker and stir in the diced tomatoes and chickpeas.
Cover and cook on low for 6 hours, or on high for 3 hours, until the chickpeas are plump and the kitchen smells like curry.
Stir in the coconut milk during the last 20 minutes of cooking rather than at the start — coconut milk can turn grainy and separate after hours of slow simmering.
Stir in the spinach, cover, and let it wilt in the residual heat, about 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve warm.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, heat the olive oil, and cook the onion until soft and golden, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, and curry powder, stirring until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and chickpeas, holding back the coconut milk for now — it can curdle under high heat and pressure.
Lock the lid and cook on high pressure for 5 minutes.
Quick release the pressure right away so the sauce doesn't keep cooking longer than it needs to.
Switch back to sauté, stir in the coconut milk and spinach, and simmer uncovered just until the spinach wilts and everything is heated through, about 3 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve warm.
Combine the olive oil, onion, garlic, cumin, and chili powder directly in the slow cooker — there's no need to sauté first, since low heat will soften the onion and bloom the spices over time.
Add the black beans along with a splash of water, stirring to coat them in the spiced oil.
Cover and cook on low for 3 hours, or on high for 1 1/2 hours, until the onion is completely soft and the beans have soaked up the spices.
Mash about half the beans right in the slow cooker with a fork, leaving the rest whole for texture.
Stir in the lime juice and season with salt and pepper.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet, about 20 seconds per side, until soft and pliable.
Fill each tortilla with the black bean mixture and top with avocado and cilantro before serving.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, heat the olive oil, and cook the onion until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, and chili powder, stirring until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add the black beans with a splash of water, scraping up anything stuck to the bottom of the pot.
Lock the lid and cook on high pressure for 3 minutes — just long enough for the beans to soak up the spices without turning to mush.
Quick release the pressure, then mash about half the beans right in the pot with a fork, leaving the rest whole for texture.
Stir in the lime juice and season with salt and pepper.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet, about 20 seconds per side, until soft and pliable.
Fill each tortilla with the black bean mixture and top with avocado and cilantro before serving.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add the garlic and cumin, stirring until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Stir in the rice, black beans, diced tomatoes, and half the cheddar cheese, then season with salt and pepper.

Spoon the filling into each pepper, packing it in gently and mounding slightly at the top — no need to parboil the peppers first, since the air fryer's strong circulating heat will cook them through on its own.
Preheat the air fryer to 350°F for 3 minutes.
Working in batches of 2 so each pepper stands upright with room for air to move around it, place the peppers in the basket and air fry for 18 minutes, until tender when pierced with a knife.
Sprinkle the remaining cheddar cheese over the peppers and air fry until melted, about 3 more minutes.
Move the finished peppers to a plate and repeat the last two steps with the remaining peppers, since the basket needs open space around each one to cook evenly.
Serve the peppers warm, spooning any juices left on the plate over the top.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add the garlic and cumin, stirring until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Stir in the rice, black beans, diced tomatoes, and half the cheddar cheese, then season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the filling into each pepper, packing it in gently and mounding slightly at the top.
Pour a little water into the bottom of the slow cooker, just enough to cover the base, and stand the stuffed peppers up inside, nestling them close together so they support one another.
Cover and cook on low for 6 hours, or on high for 3 hours, until the peppers are completely tender.
Sprinkle the remaining cheddar cheese over the tops, cover again, and cook just until melted, about 10 minutes.
Lift the peppers out carefully with tongs and serve warm.
Heat the griddle to medium-high and drizzle on 1 tablespoon of the vegetable oil, spreading it thin across the surface.
Pour the eggs onto one section of the griddle and scramble with a spatula until just set, breaking them into small pieces, then push them to a cooler section.
Drizzle a little more oil onto an open section, add the carrot, and cook, stirring, until slightly softened, about 2 minutes.
Add the frozen peas and garlic to the same section and cook until the peas are bright and heated through, about 2 minutes.
Push everything to one side, drizzle the remaining oil onto the open space, and spread the cold rice across the hot griddle in a thin layer so it makes good contact and crisps instead of steaming.
Let the rice sit undisturbed for a minute to pick up some char, then break up any clumps and toss everything together, stir-frying until heated through, about 4 minutes.
Fold the scrambled eggs back in, drizzle the soy sauce and sesame oil over the top, and toss until evenly coated.
Scatter the green onions over the top and serve hot right off the griddle.
Lay the eggplant slices on paper towels, sprinkle both sides with salt, and let sit for 15 minutes to draw out excess moisture, then pat dry.
Set up three shallow dishes: one with flour, one with the beaten eggs, and one with the breadcrumbs mixed with the parmesan cheese.
Dip each eggplant slice in flour, then egg, then the breadcrumb mixture, pressing gently so it sticks.
Preheat the air fryer to 375°F, then lightly brush both sides of the breaded slices with olive oil — this stands in for the frying oil and is what gets them golden and crisp.
Working in batches so the slices sit in a single layer without touching, air fry for 10 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and crisp.
Repeat with the remaining batches, keeping the finished slices on a rack nearby.

Spread a thin layer of marinara sauce in a small air-fryer-safe baking dish, then layer in eggplant slices, more sauce, and a scatter of mozzarella cheese, repeating until everything is used — you may need two smaller dishes rather than one large one.
Air fry at 350°F until the cheese is melted and golden and the sauce is bubbling at the edges, about 8 minutes.
Let it rest for 5 minutes, then scatter the basil over the top before serving.
Lay the eggplant slices on paper towels, sprinkle both sides with salt, and let sit for 15 minutes to draw out excess moisture, then pat dry.
Set up three shallow dishes: one with flour, one with the beaten eggs, and one with the breadcrumbs mixed with the parmesan cheese.
Dip each eggplant slice in flour, then egg, then the breadcrumb mixture, pressing firmly so the coating can hold up to the grill grates.
Heat the grill to medium and oil the grates well, using a folded paper towel dipped in olive oil and held with tongs — a well-oiled grate is what keeps the breading from tearing away.
Grill the breaded slices directly on the grate, working in batches, until deep golden grill marks form and the coating sets, about 4 minutes per side.
Move the grilled slices to a tray as each batch finishes.
In a grill-safe baking dish, spread a thin layer of marinara sauce, then layer in the grilled eggplant, more sauce, and a scatter of mozzarella cheese, repeating until everything is used.
Set the dish on the grill grates, close the lid, and cook over indirect heat until the cheese is melted and the sauce bubbles at the edges, about 12 minutes.
Let it rest for 5 minutes off the heat, then scatter the basil over the top before serving.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion, carrots, and celery until softened, about 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and cumin, stirring until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Scrape the mixture into the slow cooker.
Stir in the lentils, diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, and bay leaf.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, or on high for 4 hours, until the lentils are fully tender and the soup has thickened.
Remove the bay leaf and season with salt and pepper before serving.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, heat the olive oil, and cook the onion, carrots, and celery until softened, about 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and cumin, stirring until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Stir in the lentils, diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, and bay leaf, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Lock the lid and cook on high pressure for 15 minutes — dried lentils go from raw to tender in a fraction of the stovetop time.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes before opening the valve — releasing it quickly can cause the soup to sputter out through the vent.
Remove the bay leaf and season with salt and pepper before serving.
Beat the butter, brown sugar, and granulated sugar together in a large bowl until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in the vanilla extract until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, and salt.
Stir the dry ingredients into the butter mixture just until no streaks of flour remain.
Fold in the chocolate chips so they are spread evenly through the dough.

Cut a piece of parchment paper to fit the air fryer basket and preheat the air fryer to 325°F — about 25 degrees cooler than the oven, since air fryers cook hotter and faster than their dial suggests.
Drop rounded tablespoons of dough onto the parchment, leaving space between each — a standard basket only holds about 6 cookies at a time, so plan on baking in rounds.
Air fry until the edges are golden but the centers still look slightly underdone, 7 to 8 minutes, checking a minute early since air fryers vary.
Let the cookies rest on the parchment for 5 minutes before moving them to a wire rack, then repeat with the remaining dough in batches.
Melt the butter in a small saucepan over low heat, then remove from the heat and whisk in the cocoa powder until smooth.
Whisk in the granulated sugar, then the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla extract, whisking hard after each addition until the batter looks glossy.
Sprinkle the flour and salt over the batter and fold in gently with a spatula, stopping as soon as the flour disappears.
Stir in the chocolate chips.
Line a 6-inch round cake pan with parchment paper, leaving an overhang to lift the brownies out later — this smaller size is what actually fits inside most air fryer baskets.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan, smooth the top, and preheat the air fryer to 325°F for 3 minutes.

Set the pan in the basket and air fry until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out with a few moist crumbs, 30 to 35 minutes — loosely tent the top with foil partway through if it's browning faster than the center is setting.
Cool the brownies completely in the pan before lifting them out by the parchment overhang and cutting into squares.
Whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt in a medium bowl.
In a large bowl, whisk the vegetable oil, granulated sugar, and brown sugar together, then beat in the eggs one at a time until the mixture is smooth and light.
Stir the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients until just combined, then fold in the grated carrots.
Grease two 6-inch round cake pans — the size that actually fits an air fryer basket — and line the bottoms with parchment paper.
Divide the batter evenly between the two pans, then preheat the air fryer to 325°F — most baskets only have room to bake one 6-inch pan at a time.
Air fry the first pan until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, 25 to 28 minutes, then repeat with the second pan.
Cool the cakes in their pans for 10 minutes, then turn them out onto a wire rack and cool completely before frosting.
Beat the cream cheese and butter together in a clean bowl until smooth, then add the powdered sugar and beat until the frosting is fluffy and holds its shape.
Set one cake layer on a plate, spread a thick layer of frosting on top, stack the second layer, then frost the top and sides of the whole cake.
Beat the butter and granulated sugar together in a large bowl until pale and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Beat in the egg and vanilla extract until fully combined.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, and salt together in a separate bowl, then mix into the butter mixture until a soft dough forms.
Shape the dough into a disk, wrap it, and refrigerate until firm, at least 1 hour.
Roll the dough out on a lightly floured surface to about 1/4-inch thickness and cut into shapes.
Cut a piece of parchment paper to fit the air fryer basket and preheat the air fryer to 325°F.
Arrange as many cookies as fit without touching — usually about 6 — on the parchment in the basket, and air fry until the edges are just barely golden, 6 to 7 minutes.
Let the cookies cool on the parchment for 5 minutes, then move them to a wire rack, and repeat with the remaining dough in batches before decorating.
Stir the peanut butter and granulated sugar together in a large bowl until smooth.
Mix in the egg, vanilla extract, baking soda, and salt until a soft dough comes together.
Roll the dough into 1-inch balls, then roll each ball in a little extra granulated sugar.
Cut a piece of parchment paper to fit the air fryer basket and preheat the air fryer to 325°F.
Place the balls on the parchment a couple inches apart — about 6 at a time in most baskets — then press a crosshatch pattern into each with a fork.
Air fry until the edges are set but the centers still look soft, 7 to 8 minutes — they will firm up as they cool.
Cool the cookies on the parchment for 5 minutes before moving them to a wire rack, then repeat with the remaining dough in batches.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl and set aside.
Beat the butter and granulated sugar together until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla extract.
Add the flour mixture and milk in alternating additions, mixing just until smooth after each.
Line silicone muffin cups with paper liners — silicone holds up to the air fryer basket better than a standard metal pan, which usually won't fit.
Fill 4 to 5 cups about two-thirds full, preheat the air fryer to 325°F, and set the filled cups in the basket.
Air fry until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, 11 to 13 minutes.
Cool the cupcakes for 5 minutes, then move them to a wire rack, and repeat with the remaining batter in batches — a full dozen usually takes about three rounds.
Once completely cool, frost with the powdered sugar buttercream.
Toss the sliced apples with the granulated sugar, lemon juice, and half the cinnamon.
In a separate bowl, mix the rolled oats, flour, brown sugar, remaining cinnamon, and salt together.
Cut the cold butter into the oat mixture with your fingers or a fork until it looks like coarse, clumpy crumbs.
Grease a small baking dish that fits inside your air fryer basket, about 6 to 7 inches across, and spread the apples in an even layer.
Scatter the topping evenly over the apples.
Preheat the air fryer to 350°F for 3 minutes.

Set the dish in the basket and air fry until the topping is deep golden and the apples are bubbling at the edges, 22 to 25 minutes — check at 20 minutes, since the topping can go from golden to too dark quickly in the strong airflow.
Let the crisp rest for 10 minutes before serving so the juices can settle.
Beat the butter, brown sugar, and granulated sugar together until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla extract.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt together in a separate bowl, then stir into the butter mixture until just combined.
Fold in the rolled oats and raisins until evenly distributed through the dough.
Cut a piece of parchment paper to fit the air fryer basket and preheat the air fryer to 325°F.
Drop rounded tablespoons of dough onto the parchment, spacing them apart — about 6 fit per batch.
Air fry until the edges are golden and the centers look set, 8 to 9 minutes.
Cool the cookies on the parchment for 5 minutes before moving them to a wire rack, then repeat with the remaining dough in batches.
Beat the butter and 1 cup of the granulated sugar together until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla extract.
Whisk the flour, cream of tartar, baking soda, and salt together in a separate bowl, then mix into the wet ingredients until a soft dough forms.
Stir the remaining 1/2 cup granulated sugar and the cinnamon together in a small shallow bowl.
Roll the dough into 1-inch balls, then roll each ball in the cinnamon sugar until fully coated.
Cut a piece of parchment paper to fit the air fryer basket and preheat the air fryer to 325°F.
Arrange the balls on the parchment, spacing them apart — about 6 per batch — and air fry until the tops crackle and the edges just set, 7 to 8 minutes.
Cool the cookies on the parchment for 5 minutes before moving them to a wire rack, then repeat with the remaining dough in batches.
Rub the butter over the bottom and sides of the slow cooker insert — this keeps the custard from sticking to the hot ceramic as it cooks.
Spread the cubed bread in an even layer in the buttered insert.
Whisk the milk, heavy cream, eggs, granulated sugar, vanilla extract, and cinnamon together in a bowl until smooth.
Scatter the raisins over the bread, then pour the custard on top and press the bread down gently so it all soaks in.
Let it sit for 10 minutes so the bread fully absorbs the custard before cooking starts.

Cover and cook on low, tucking a folded paper towel under the lid to catch condensation so it doesn't drip back onto the pudding — a slow cooker traps steam that an oven simply vents away. Cook until the center is just set and a knife comes out with only a few moist crumbs, about 2 hours 45 minutes.
Drizzle the melted butter over the top and let the pudding rest, still covered, for 10 minutes — it won't brown like an oven-baked version, but the low heat keeps every bite ultra custardy.
Serve warm, spooned straight from the insert.
Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment paper, leaving an overhang on two sides for easy lifting later.
Combine the chocolate chips, sweetened condensed milk, and butter in a large microwave-safe bowl.

Microwave on high in 30-second bursts, stirring well after each one, until fully melted and glossy, about 2 minutes total — microwaves heat unevenly, and stirring between bursts keeps the chocolate from scorching or seizing.
Stir in the vanilla extract and salt until fully blended.
Stir in the walnuts if using, then pour the fudge into the prepared pan and smooth the top.
Refrigerate until firm, at least 2 hours, before lifting it out by the parchment and cutting into squares.
Toss the sliced strawberries with 2 tablespoons of the granulated sugar and let them sit until juicy, at least 20 minutes.
Whisk the flour, remaining granulated sugar, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl.
Cut the cold butter into the flour mixture with your fingers or a fork until it looks like coarse crumbs.

Stir in 3/4 cup of the heavy cream just until a shaggy dough forms, then pat it out on a floured surface and cut into 6 small rounds — smaller rounds cook more evenly in an air fryer basket than one large batch.
Preheat the air fryer to 330°F and arrange the rounds in the basket with space between them, in two batches if they don't all fit — crowding blocks the hot air and leaves the centers doughy.
Air fry until golden and puffed, about 9 minutes, checking a couple minutes early since air fryers run hotter and faster than an oven.
Whip the remaining heavy cream with the vanilla extract until soft peaks form.
Split the biscuits, spoon the sugared strawberries and their juices over the bottoms, top with whipped cream, and set the tops back on.
In an oven-safe ramekin or mug, whisk the flour, granulated sugar, cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt together until no lumps remain.
Add the milk, vegetable oil, and vanilla extract, and stir until the batter is smooth.
Drop the chocolate chips into the batter and give it one more quick stir.
Preheat the air fryer to 320°F — a quick preheat keeps the outside from setting before the inside has a chance to rise.

Place the ramekin in the basket and air fry until the cake has risen and the top springs back but the center is still a little soft, about 9 minutes — check at 8 minutes, since air fryers run hotter than a microwave and can dry the cake out fast.
Carefully lift out the ramekin (it will be very hot) and let it sit for 1 minute before eating.

Melt 2 tablespoons of the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion, stirring now and then, until soft and see-through, about 5 minutes — softening it on the stovetop first gives more flavor than a slow cooker alone would.
Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds, just until fragrant, then transfer the onion and garlic to the slow cooker.

Add the crushed tomatoes, sugar, only half the vegetable broth, and season with salt and pepper — slow cookers don't evaporate liquid the way a simmering pot does, so starting with less broth keeps the soup from turning thin.
Cover and cook on low until the tomatoes have fully broken down and taste sweet rather than raw, about 4 hours (or high for 2 hours).
Blend the soup smooth with an immersion blender directly in the insert, then stir in the remaining broth and the cream.
Cover and cook on low for 15 more minutes to heat the cream through gently — added at the end, it won't have a chance to break over a long cook.
While the soup finishes, butter one side of each bread slice and layer two slices of cheddar between the unbuttered sides for each sandwich.
Toast the sandwiches in a skillet over medium heat, buttered side down, until deep golden and the cheese is melting, about 3 minutes per side.
Slice the sandwiches on the diagonal and serve alongside bowls of the hot soup for dunking.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, melt 2 tablespoons of the butter, and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, just until fragrant.
Add the crushed tomatoes, the remaining broth, and the sugar, season with salt and pepper, and scrape the bottom well — any stuck bits can trigger a scorch warning once the pot pressurizes.
Lock the lid and pressure cook on high for 5 minutes, allowing about 10 minutes for the pot to come up to pressure first.
Quick release the pressure, keeping your hands and face clear of the steam, then open the lid once the pin drops.

Turn the pot off, blend the soup smooth with an immersion blender directly in the pot, then stir in the cream and let it warm on the keep-warm setting — the gentle heat won't scald it the way a hard boil would.
While the soup pressurizes, butter one side of each bread slice and layer two slices of cheddar between the unbuttered sides for each sandwich.
Toast the sandwiches in a skillet over medium heat, buttered side down, until deep golden and the cheese is melting, about 3 minutes per side.
Slice the sandwiches on the diagonal and ladle the soup into bowls to serve together for dunking.

Combine the olive oil, onion, carrots, celery, garlic, zucchini, diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, kidney beans, italian seasoning, and salt and pepper directly in the slow cooker — no need to soften anything first, the long cook does that work for you.
Cover and cook on low until the vegetables are fork-tender and the broth tastes deeply savory, about 7 hours (or high for 3 hours 30 minutes).
About 20 minutes before serving, stir in the pasta and switch the cooker to high — added earlier, the pasta would turn to mush over such a long, slow cook.
Cover and cook until the pasta is just tender, about 20 minutes.
Turn off the heat, stir in the spinach, and let it wilt in the residual warmth, about 3 minutes.
Taste, adjust the seasoning, and ladle into bowls to serve hot.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, warm the olive oil, and cook the onion, carrots, and celery until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and zucchini and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, kidney beans, and italian seasoning, season with salt and pepper, and scrape the bottom of the pot well.
Lock the lid and pressure cook on high for 3 minutes, allowing about 10 minutes for the pot to come up to pressure, then quick release.

Switch the pot to sauté, stir in the pasta, and cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until just tender, about 8 minutes — cooking pasta under pressure would turn it to mush, so it finishes here instead.
Turn off the pot, stir in the spinach, and let it wilt in the residual heat, about 2 minutes.
Taste, adjust the seasoning, and serve hot.

Combine the olive oil, onion, garlic, chili powder, cumin, diced tomatoes, chicken broth, chicken breasts, and salt and pepper in the slow cooker — no need to sauté first, the long cook blooms the spices and softens the onion.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken shreds easily with a fork, about 6 hours (or high for 3 hours).
Lift the chicken onto a cutting board, shred it with two forks, and return it to the pot.
Stir in the black beans and corn, cover, and cook on high for 15 minutes — they're already cooked, so this is just to warm them through.
Meanwhile, spread the tortilla strips on a baking sheet and bake or air-fry at 400°F until crisp, about 8 minutes.
Ladle the soup into bowls, top with the crispy tortilla strips, and serve with lime wedges for squeezing.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, warm the olive oil, and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder, and cumin and cook for 1 minute, until toasty-smelling.
Add the diced tomatoes, chicken broth, chicken breasts, and salt and pepper, and scrape the bottom of the pot to loosen any stuck bits.
Lock the lid and pressure cook on high for 10 minutes, allowing about 12 minutes for the pot to build pressure first.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then quick release the rest — resting the chicken under natural pressure keeps it from turning stringy.
Lift the chicken out, shred it with two forks, and return it to the pot.
Stir in the black beans and corn and use the sauté setting to warm everything through, about 4 minutes.
Meanwhile, spread the tortilla strips on a baking sheet and bake or air-fry at 400°F until crisp, about 8 minutes.
Ladle the soup into bowls, top with the crispy tortilla strips, and serve with lime wedges.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 4 minutes.

Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute to make a roux, then whisk in a splash of the chicken broth to loosen it — building the roux on the stovetop first keeps the soup from turning grainy under gentle slow heat.
Transfer the roux to the slow cooker, add the remaining chicken broth, the broccoli, and the carrots, and season with salt and pepper.
Cover and cook on low until the broccoli is very tender, about 4 hours (or high for 2 hours).
Stir in the milk and the cheddar cheese a handful at a time, cover, and cook on low for 20 more minutes until fully melted — added at the end so the dairy doesn't break over a long cook.
For a smoother soup, blend part of it right in the insert with an immersion blender; for a chunkier one, leave it as is.
Taste, adjust the seasoning, and serve hot.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, melt the butter, and cook the onion until soft, about 4 minutes.
Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the chicken broth until smooth with no lumps.
Add the broccoli and carrots and season with salt and pepper.
Lock the lid and pressure cook on high for 1 minute, allowing about 8 minutes for the pot to build pressure — broccoli cooks fast, so a short pressure time keeps it from turning to mush.
Quick release the pressure right away to stop the broccoli from overcooking and losing its color.
With the pot off, stir in the milk and the cheddar cheese a handful at a time until melted and glossy — off heat, the cheese melts smoothly instead of breaking.
For a smoother soup, blend part of it with an immersion blender; for a chunkier one, leave it as is.
Taste, adjust the seasoning, and serve hot.

Melt the butter and olive oil in a skillet over medium heat, add the onions and sugar, and stir to coat — starting them in a hot pan with a little fat jumpstarts browning that a slow cooker alone can't reach.

Transfer the onions to the slow cooker and cook on low with the lid propped slightly ajar (a wooden spoon handle works well) until deeply golden brown and jammy, about 8 hours — the small gap lets steam escape so the onions caramelize instead of just steaming.
Stir in the garlic and flour, close the lid fully, and cook on low for 10 more minutes.
Stir in the wine, beef broth, and thyme, season with salt and pepper, and cook on low for 1 more hour so the flavors meld.
Remove the thyme sprigs.
Toast the baguette slices in the oven at 400°F until dry and lightly golden, about 8 minutes — a slow cooker can't toast or broil, so the bread and cheese still finish in the oven.
Ladle the soup into oven-safe bowls, float one or two toasted baguette slices on top of each, and pile on the gruyere.
Set the bowls on a baking sheet and broil until the cheese is melted and bubbling with brown spots, about 3 minutes — watch closely so it doesn't burn.
Let the bowls cool for a minute before serving, since the cheese and broth will be very hot.

Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the leeks until soft and bright, about 6 minutes — softening them on the stovetop first keeps their flavor clean instead of turning oniony over a long slow cook.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, just until fragrant, then transfer everything to the slow cooker.
Add the potatoes, vegetable broth, and bay leaf to the slow cooker, and season with salt and pepper.
Cover and cook on low until the potatoes are fork-tender, about 6 hours (or high for 3 hours).
Remove the bay leaf, then blend the soup smooth directly in the insert with an immersion blender.
Stir in the cream, cover, and warm on low for 10 more minutes without letting it boil — added at the end, it won't have a chance to separate over a long cook.
Taste, adjust the seasoning, ladle into bowls, and scatter the chives over the top.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté, melt the butter, and cook the leeks until soft and bright, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, just until fragrant.
Add the potatoes, vegetable broth, and bay leaf, and season with salt and pepper.
Lock the lid and pressure cook on high for 8 minutes, allowing about 10 minutes for the pot to build pressure, then quick release.
Remove the bay leaf, turn the pot off, and blend the soup smooth directly in the pot with an immersion blender.
Stir in the cream and warm it through on the sauté setting for a minute or two, without letting it boil.
Taste, adjust the seasoning, ladle into bowls, and scatter the chives over the top.
Pulse the drained chickpeas, onion, and garlic in a food processor until the mixture looks like coarse sand — don't puree it smooth or the falafel will turn dense.
Add the parsley, cilantro, cumin, and coriander and pulse again until finely chopped and evenly distributed.
Transfer to a bowl, stir in the flour and baking powder, cover, and chill in the fridge for 30 minutes to help the mixture hold together.
Shape the chilled mixture into small, slightly flattened patties, about 2 tablespoons each — flatter shapes get more surface contact with the hot air than round balls.
Preheat the air fryer to 375°F, then brush the basket and the patties lightly with the vegetable oil — you'll only need a couple tablespoons, not the full amount used for deep frying.
Arrange the patties in a single layer with space between them and air fry until deep golden and crisp, flipping once halfway, about 12 minutes.
Warm the flatbreads briefly in a dry skillet or microwave until soft and pliable.
Fill each flatbread with falafel, cucumber, and tomatoes, then drizzle generously with tahini sauce before rolling up to serve.
In a bowl, gently mix the ground turkey, breadcrumbs, onion, worcestershire sauce, egg, garlic powder, salt, and pepper until just combined — overmixing makes tough burgers.
Divide into 4 patties, pressing a shallow dimple in the center of each so they cook up flat instead of doming.
Preheat the air fryer to 375°F and brush the basket lightly with the olive oil — lean turkey is more prone to sticking than fattier ground beef.
Arrange the patties in the basket without touching and air fry for 8 minutes, then flip.
Cook the second side until the center reaches 165°F on a meat thermometer, about 7 more minutes.
Let the patties rest on a plate for 2 minutes so the juices settle back in.
Toast the burger buns in the air fryer basket for the last minute if you like, then build each burger with lettuce, tomato, and a patty.
In a bowl, gently mix the ground turkey, breadcrumbs, onion, worcestershire sauce, egg, garlic powder, salt, and pepper until just combined — overmixing makes tough burgers.
Divide into 4 patties, pressing a shallow dimple in the center of each so they cook up flat.
Heat the olive oil on the griddle over medium heat until shimmering — a griddle's flat, even surface holds a steadier temperature across several patties than a curved skillet.
Cook the patties undisturbed until deeply golden and easy to release, about 5 minutes, then flip.
Cook the second side until the center reaches 165°F on a meat thermometer, about 5 more minutes.
Let the patties rest on a plate for 2 minutes so the juices settle back in.
In the last minute, toast the burger buns cut-side down right on the griddle alongside the patties, then build each burger with lettuce, tomato, and a patty.
In a bowl, gently mix the ground turkey, breadcrumbs, onion, worcestershire sauce, egg, garlic powder, salt, and pepper until just combined — overmixing makes tough burgers.
Divide into 4 patties, pressing a shallow dimple in the center of each so they stay flat instead of puffing up on the grill.
Preheat the grill to medium-high and rub the grates with a paper towel dipped in the olive oil — lean turkey sticks to grates more than fattier ground beef, so a well-oiled grate matters here.
Grill the patties with the lid down, undisturbed, for 6 minutes — a closed lid traps heat around the patties like a mini oven, cooking them through evenly without constant flipping.
Flip and grill the second side until the center reaches 165°F on a meat thermometer, about 6 more minutes.
Move the patties to a plate and tent loosely with foil to rest for 3 minutes — outdoor heat escapes fast, so tenting keeps them warm.
In the last minute, toast the burger buns cut-side down directly on the grill grates, then build each burger with lettuce, tomato, and a patty.
Pat the chicken wings very dry with paper towels — the drier they are, the crispier they'll get.
In a bowl, toss the wings with the baking powder, garlic powder, paprika, and salt until evenly coated.
Let the wings sit uncovered on a plate in the fridge for 15 minutes to dry the skin further — this matters even more in an air fryer, where extra moisture turns to steam fast in the small basket.
Preheat the air fryer to 380°F.
Arrange half the wings in a single layer in the basket without touching — crowding traps steam and keeps them from crisping.
Air fry for 12 minutes, flip, and cook until deep golden and crackling, about 10 more minutes.
Repeat with the second batch of wings, another 20 to 22 minutes, since a single air fryer basket won't hold them all at once.
While the wings cook, whisk the hot sauce and melted butter together in a bowl.
As soon as each batch comes out of the air fryer, toss the wings in the hot sauce mixture until fully coated and glossy.
Serve immediately while hot and crackling.
Brush the baguette slices lightly with 3 tablespoons of the olive oil.
Preheat the air fryer to 375°F.

Arrange the slices in a single layer in the basket, in two batches if needed, and air fry until golden and crisp at the edges, about 4 minutes — air fryers toast bread much faster than an oven, so watch closely.
While the bread toasts, combine the tomatoes, minced garlic, basil, balsamic vinegar, and the remaining olive oil in a bowl, and season with salt and pepper.
Let the tomato mixture sit for 5 minutes so the flavors meld while the last batch of bread finishes.
As soon as the toasts come out, rub the top of each one with the whole garlic clove for a light garlic flavor.
Spoon the tomato mixture generously onto each toast just before serving so they stay crisp.
Brown the ground beef in a skillet over medium heat, breaking it up with a spoon, until no pink remains, about 6 minutes.
