Stir in the taco seasoning and a splash of water, then simmer for 2 minutes until the meat is well coated.
Preheat the air fryer to 350°F.
Line the basket with a perforated parchment liner and add a single, shallow layer of tortilla chips — nachos need to stay shallow in an air fryer, or the top melts before the bottom warms through.
Scatter the beef, cheddar cheese, and black beans evenly over the chips.
Air fry until the cheese is fully melted and bubbling, about 4 minutes, checking at 3 since air fryers run hot and chips near the top can scorch fast.
Repeat in batches with the remaining chips and toppings — a single basket won't hold a full sheet-pan's worth at once.
Top with the tomato, jalapeno, dollops of sour cream, and green onions, then serve immediately while hot.
Cut the cream cheese into cubes so it melts faster and more evenly once it's in the slow cooker.
Combine the spinach, artichoke hearts, cubed cream cheese, sour cream, and mayonnaise in the slow cooker insert.
Stir in the garlic, parmesan cheese, and half of the mozzarella cheese, and season with salt and pepper.
Cover and cook on low, stirring once halfway through, until fully melted and hot throughout, about 2 hours — no oven preheat needed, and the low heat won't scorch the cheese the way a hot oven can.
Sprinkle the remaining mozzarella over the top, cover, and cook for 10 more minutes until melted.
Switch to the warm setting once it's ready — this is the real advantage of a slow cooker dip, staying hot and party-ready for hours without drying out.
Serve warm with crackers, straight from the insert.
Unroll the crescent dough onto a cutting board, separate along the perforations into triangles, and cut each triangle lengthwise into 3 thin strips.
Wrap a strip of dough around each cocktail sausage in a spiral, tucking the ends underneath to hold it in place.
Preheat the air fryer to 350°F.
Arrange the wrapped sausages in a single layer in the basket, leaving space between each one — the dough puffs as it cooks, and pieces that touch will fuse together.
Brush each one with the beaten egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds if using.
Air fry until puffed and deep golden, about 7 minutes, checking at 6 since the dough can go from golden to too dark quickly.
Repeat with the remaining batches — a basket typically holds about half a batch at a time, so plan on cooking in two rounds.
Let them cool for a minute or two, then serve warm with yellow mustard for dipping.
Stir the warm water and sugar together in a bowl, sprinkle the yeast over the top, and let it sit until foamy, about 5 minutes.
Add the flour, kosher salt, and melted butter, then mix and knead until you have a smooth, elastic dough, about 6 minutes.
Shape the dough into a ball, place it in an oiled bowl, cover, and let it rise in a warm spot until doubled, about 40 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces, roll each into a rope about 24 inches, and twist into a pretzel shape.

Bring a pot of water to a boil and stir in the baking soda carefully, since it will fizz — this step still happens on the stovetop, since it's the chemistry that gives pretzels their chewy crust, not something an air fryer can replace.
Boil each pretzel for 20 seconds per side, then use a slotted spoon to transfer it to a tray.
Preheat the air fryer to 350°F, brush each pretzel with the beaten egg, and sprinkle generously with the pretzel salt.
Arrange 2 to 3 pretzels at a time in the basket without touching and air fry until deeply golden, about 6 minutes — air fryers run hotter and more concentrated than an oven, so watch closely.
Repeat in batches until all the pretzels are cooked, about 18 more minutes total.
Cool the pretzels for a few minutes on a wire rack before serving warm.
Combine the chicken breasts and chicken broth in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken shreds easily with a fork, about 4 hours (or high for 2 hours).

Lift the chicken out, shred it with two forks, and pour off most of the broth — a slow cooker doesn't reduce liquid the way a stovetop simmer does, so draining the extra keeps the dip from turning watery.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the cream cheese, hot sauce, ranch dressing, and half of the cheddar cheese.
Cover and cook on low for 20 more minutes, stirring once, until the cream cheese is fully melted and smooth.
Sprinkle the remaining cheddar cheese on top, cover, and cook for 10 more minutes until melted.
Switch to the warm setting — the dip stays hot for serving all party long without drying out the way an oven-baked version would.
Garnish with the green onions and serve with celery sticks for dipping.
Soak the potato wedges in a bowl of cold water for 10 minutes to rinse away surface starch — this is what lets them crisp in the air fryer instead of turning soft.
Drain and pat the wedges completely dry with a clean towel — any leftover water turns to steam and stops browning.
Toss the wedges with olive oil, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and black pepper until evenly coated.
Preheat the air fryer to 380°F for 3 minutes.
Arrange half the wedges in a single layer in the basket, skin-side down — crowding is the enemy of crisp edges here.
Air fry the first batch until deeply golden and crisp, shaking the basket halfway, about 16 to 18 minutes.
Repeat with the second batch of wedges, shaking halfway, until just as golden and crisp.
Combine both batches, sprinkle with parsley, and serve hot.
Pat the chicken breasts dry and rub both sides with the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, and salt.
Preheat a grill to medium-high heat and oil the grates.
Meanwhile, warm the salsa in a small saucepan over medium heat until simmering, about 5 minutes — this stands in for the sauce a slow cooker would build on its own.
Grill the chicken with the lid down until deep grill marks form and the thickest part reaches 165°F, about 6 minutes per side.
Move the chicken to a cutting board and rest 5 minutes so the juices settle back in.
Slice or shred the chicken, then spoon the warm salsa over the top and squeeze in the lime juice.
Serve warm in tortillas, over rice, or piled onto nachos.
Place the chicken breasts in the pressure cooker in a single layer.
Pour the salsa over the chicken, then sprinkle on the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, and salt.
Seal the lid and cook on high pressure for 12 minutes — plenty of time for the chicken to turn fork-tender without drying out.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then quick-release any that's left — natural release keeps the chicken from seizing up.
Shred the chicken right in the pot, stir it through the sauce, and squeeze in the lime juice. Taste and adjust salt.
Serve warm in tortillas, over rice, or piled onto nachos.
Pat the chicken breasts dry and season with the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, and salt on both sides.
Spread half the salsa over the bottom of a large skillet and set the chicken on top in a single layer.
Pour the remaining salsa over the chicken, cover, and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer, covered, flipping once, until the chicken reaches 165°F and shreds easily, about 18 to 20 minutes.
Transfer the chicken to a plate, shred with two forks, then stir it back into the skillet sauce with the lime juice. Taste and adjust salt.
Serve warm in tortillas, over rice, or piled onto nachos.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté and brown the ground beef with the onion and garlic until the meat is no longer pink, about 8 minutes. Drain excess fat.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, kidney beans, chili powder, cumin, salt, and black pepper.
Seal the lid and cook on high pressure for 8 minutes — just enough to marry the flavors since the beef and beans are already cooked.
Quick-release the pressure once the timer ends.
Switch back to sauté and simmer uncovered a few minutes until the chili reaches the thickness you like.
Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed. Ladle into bowls and top as you like.
In a bowl, whisk together the honey, soy sauce, ketchup, garlic, and ginger until smooth.
Add the frozen meatballs to the pressure cooker and pour the sauce over the top without stirring — a little sauce touching the bottom helps the pot come to pressure.
Seal the lid and cook on high pressure for 5 minutes — frozen meatballs only need enough time to heat through and soak up the sauce.
Quick-release the pressure.
Switch to sauté and simmer uncovered, stirring gently, until the sauce thickens to a glossy glaze, about 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir once more, sprinkle with sesame seeds, and serve over rice or with toothpicks.
In a large skillet over medium heat, whisk together the honey, soy sauce, ketchup, garlic, and ginger until smooth and starting to bubble.
Add the frozen meatballs and stir to coat them in the sauce.
Cover and simmer over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until the meatballs are heated through, about 12 to 15 minutes.
Uncover and simmer a few minutes more until the sauce clings to the meatballs in a glossy coat.
Stir once more, sprinkle with sesame seeds, and serve over rice or with toothpicks.
Add the dried lentils, carrot, onion, celery, diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, garlic, thyme, salt, and black pepper to the pressure cooker.
Stir to combine, seal the lid, and cook on high pressure for 10 minutes — lentils go from raw to tender fast under pressure, no all-day simmer needed.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then quick-release any that's left.
Stir in the spinach and let it wilt in the residual heat with the lid ajar, about 2 minutes.
Taste for salt and pepper, then ladle into bowls.
Combine the dried lentils, carrot, onion, celery, diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, garlic, thyme, salt, and black pepper in a large pot.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a gentle simmer and cover partway.
Simmer, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender and the stew has thickened, about 30 to 35 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and cook just until wilted, about 2 minutes.
Taste for salt and pepper, then ladle into bowls.
Pat the ribs dry. Mix the brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper, then rub all over the ribs.
Set the ribs in the pressure cooker on the trivet, curling them to fit, and pour the apple cider vinegar and a splash of water into the bottom — the liquid is what lets the pot build steam.
Seal the lid and cook on high pressure for 25 minutes — ribs turn fall-off-the-bone tender in a fraction of the slow cooker's time.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then quick-release the rest.
Carefully lift the ribs onto a foil-lined baking sheet and brush with half the BBQ sauce.
Broil 3 to 4 minutes until the sauce bubbles and starts to caramelize, then brush with the remaining BBQ sauce.
Rest a few minutes, then cut into portions and serve with extra napkins.
Preheat the oven to 300°F and pat the ribs dry.
Mix the brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper, then rub all over the ribs.
Wrap the ribs tightly in foil with the apple cider vinegar drizzled inside — the sealed foil traps steam so the ribs braise in their own liquid, much like a slow cooker does.
Bake until the meat has pulled back from the bone ends and is fork-tender, about 2 1/2 hours.
Carefully open the foil, watching for steam, brush the ribs with half the BBQ sauce, and raise the oven to 425°F.
Bake uncovered until the sauce sets and starts to caramelize at the edges, about 12 to 15 minutes.
Brush with the remaining BBQ sauce, rest a few minutes, then cut into portions.
Serve with extra napkins — these are messy in the best way.
Pat the chicken thighs dry and rub all over with the taco seasoning.
Preheat a grill to medium-high heat and oil the grates.
Meanwhile, simmer the onion, green chiles, and chicken broth in a small saucepan over medium heat until the onion softens, about 6 minutes.
Grill the chicken thighs, lid down, until charred and the thickest part reaches 165°F, about 5 to 6 minutes per side.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes, then slice or shred it.
Toss the chicken with the warm onion-chile broth, then stir in the lime juice and cilantro.
Spoon into warm tortillas or bowls and load up your favorite toppings.
Scatter the onion in the bottom of the pressure cooker and set the chicken thighs on top.
Sprinkle the taco seasoning over the chicken, then add the green chiles and chicken broth.
Seal the lid and cook on high pressure for 10 minutes — thighs turn shreddy-tender fast under pressure.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then quick-release the rest.
Shred the chicken right in the pot, stir through the juices, then mix in the lime juice and cilantro.
Spoon into warm tortillas or bowls and load up your favorite toppings.
Heat the chicken broth in a large skillet over medium heat, add the onion, and cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Nestle the chicken thighs into the skillet, sprinkle the taco seasoning over the top, and add the green chiles.
Cover and simmer over medium-low heat, flipping once, until the chicken reaches 165°F and shreds easily, about 20 to 22 minutes.
Transfer the chicken to a plate and shred with two forks, then stir it back into the skillet with the pan juices.
Mix in the lime juice and cilantro.
Spoon into warm tortillas or bowls and load up your favorite toppings.
Preheat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Pat the salmon fillets dry, brush with olive oil, and season with garlic powder, salt, and black pepper.
Place the salmon skin-side down on the baking sheet. Squeeze lemon juice over the top and lay a lemon slice on each fillet.
Bake until the salmon flakes easily with a fork and looks opaque in the center, about 12 to 14 minutes — a few minutes longer than the air fryer since the oven heats more gently around the fish.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve immediately.
Set up three shallow dishes: flour mixed with half the salt; beaten eggs; and breadcrumbs mixed with paprika, garlic powder, and remaining salt.
Dredge each chicken tender in flour, dip in egg, then press into the breadcrumb mix until coated.
Preheat the oven to 425°F and set a wire rack inside a baking sheet — the rack lets air move underneath so the bottom crisps instead of steaming.
Arrange the tenders on the rack in a single layer and mist both sides with cooking spray.
Bake until deep golden and the thickest piece reaches 165°F, about 18 to 20 minutes, flipping halfway.
Rest 2 minutes so the crust stays crisp, then serve with your favorite dip.
Pat the firm tofu cubes very dry with paper towels.
In a bowl, toss the tofu with soy sauce, maple syrup, sesame oil, and garlic powder. Sprinkle on cornstarch and toss until every cube looks dusty and coated.
Preheat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Spread the tofu in a single layer with space between the pieces — crowding traps steam and keeps the oven from browning it the way the air fryer's tight airflow does.
Bake until deeply golden and crisp on the edges, flipping once halfway, about 28 to 30 minutes.
Top with scallions and serve over rice or in a grain bowl.
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Pat the shrimp dry and toss with melted butter, garlic, paprika, salt, and black pepper.
Spread the shrimp in a single layer in a baking dish.
Bake until pink, curled, and opaque all the way through, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Toss with lemon juice and parsley right in the dish, then serve straight from the oven over pasta, rice, or salad.
Pat the shrimp dry and toss with melted butter, garlic, paprika, salt, and black pepper.
Preheat the broiler and set an oven rack about 6 inches from the heat.
Spread the shrimp in a single layer on a sheet pan, leaving space between each piece so they char instead of steam.
Broil until pink, curled, and lightly charred at the edges, about 4 to 5 minutes — watch closely, broilers work fast.
Toss with lemon juice and parsley right on the pan. Serve right away over pasta, rice, or salad.
Add the dried black beans, onion, garlic, cumin, chili powder, vegetable broth, diced tomatoes, and salt to the slow cooker. Stir well.
Cover and cook on low until the beans are fully tender and starting to fall apart, about 8 hours — no overnight soak needed, the slow cooker just takes its place.
Mash a cup of beans against the side of the pot to thicken the soup.
Stir in the lime juice and taste for salt. Serve hot.
Add the dried black beans, onion, garlic, cumin, chili powder, vegetable broth, diced tomatoes, and salt to a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a low simmer and cover partway.
Simmer, stirring occasionally and adding a splash more broth if it thickens too fast, until the beans are fully tender, about 1 1/2 to 2 hours — unsoaked beans just need the extra time on the stove.
Mash a cup of beans against the side of the pot to thicken.
Stir in the lime juice and taste for salt. Serve hot.
Place the chicken breasts in the slow cooker.
Add the chicken broth, apple cider vinegar, brown sugar, garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt, and half the BBQ sauce.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken shreds easily with two forks, about 5 hours (or 3 hours on high).
Transfer the chicken to a board and shred with two forks — it should pull apart with almost no resistance.
Return the chicken to the pot, stir in the remaining BBQ sauce, and let it sit uncovered a few minutes to soak in.
Serve on buns or over rice.
Place the chicken breasts in a large skillet.
Add the chicken broth, apple cider vinegar, brown sugar, garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt, and half the BBQ sauce.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook over medium-low heat, flipping once, until the chicken reaches 165°F and shreds easily, about 22 to 25 minutes.
Transfer the chicken to a board and shred with two forks.
Return the chicken to the skillet, stir in the remaining BBQ sauce, and simmer uncovered 2 minutes until glossy.
Serve on buns or over rice.
In a skillet on the stovetop, cook the bacon until crisp, about 6 minutes. Scoop out most of it and set aside, leaving a little fat behind — a slow cooker can't crisp bacon on its own.
Add the onion and garlic to the same skillet and cook until soft, about 3 minutes.
Transfer the bacon fat, onion, and garlic to the slow cooker along with the russet potatoes, chicken broth, salt, and black pepper.
Cover and cook on low until the potatoes are fork-tender, about 6 hours (or 3 hours on high).
Mash some of the potatoes against the side of the pot until the soup looks thick but still chunky.
Stir in the milk, sour cream, and cheddar cheese until melted and creamy. Taste for salt.
Ladle into bowls and top with the reserved bacon and scallions.
In a large pot, cook the bacon until crisp, about 6 minutes. Scoop out most of it and set aside, leaving a little fat in the pot.
Add the onion and garlic; cook until soft, about 3 minutes.
Add the russet potatoes, chicken broth, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer.
Simmer, partially covered, until the potatoes are fork-tender, about 18 to 20 minutes.
Mash some of the potatoes against the side of the pot until the soup looks thick but still chunky.
Stir in the milk, sour cream, and cheddar cheese until melted and creamy. Taste for salt.
Ladle into bowls and top with reserved bacon and scallions.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and sear the italian sausage links on all sides until browned, about 5 minutes — this is the flavor step a slow cooker can't do on its own.
Toss the bell peppers and onion with the garlic powder, italian seasoning, salt, and black pepper, then spread them in the bottom of the slow cooker.
Nestle the browned sausage on top of the vegetables.
Cover and cook on low until the peppers are soft and the sausage reaches 165°F, about 4 hours (or 2 to 2 1/2 hours on high).
Rest 3 minutes, then slice the sausage and serve with the peppers on rolls or over rice.

Pat the chicken thighs dry, then rub with half the olive oil, half the lemon juice, half the garlic, the oregano, and half the salt and pepper. Let it sit at room temperature while the grill heats — resting helps the chicken cook evenly.
Toss the potatoes with the remaining olive oil, salt, and pepper, then thread them onto skewers so they don't fall through the grill grates.
Heat the grill to medium-high, about 400°F, and clean and oil the grates so the chicken skin won't stick.

Grill the potato skewers over direct heat, turning occasionally, until they pick up char marks and are tender when pierced with a knife, about 15 minutes. Move them to a cooler part of the grill to keep warm.
Place the chicken thighs skin-side down over direct heat and grill without moving them until the skin is deep golden and releases easily from the grates, about 8 minutes.
Flip the thighs, move them to a cooler part of the grill if flare-ups happen, close the lid, and keep cooking until the thickest part reaches 165°F, about 12 more minutes.
In the last two minutes, lay the lemon slices directly on the grates alongside the chicken so they soften and pick up light char.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes, then squeeze the charred lemon over the chicken and potatoes and serve.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F for 3 minutes.
Toss the asparagus with half the olive oil, half the salt, and half the black pepper.
Brush the salmon fillets with the remaining olive oil, garlic, and lemon juice, and season with the remaining salt and pepper. Top with lemon slices.
Air fry the asparagus alone in a single layer until bright green and crisp-tender, about 6 minutes, then move it to a plate — the basket is too crowded to fit the fish alongside.
Add the salmon fillets to the basket skin-side down in a single layer and air fry until they flake easily with a fork, about 9 minutes depending on thickness.
Return the asparagus to the basket for the final minute just to warm it back through.
Scatter the dill over the salmon and asparagus and serve.
Pat the roast dry and season all over with salt and black pepper.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté and sear the roast on all sides in its own rendered fat until deeply browned, about 8 minutes total — this crust is where a lot of the flavor comes from.
Remove the roast, add the onion, carrots, and potatoes to the pot, and stir them through the browned bits for a minute.

Whisk the beef broth with the tomato paste, garlic, and thyme, then pour it in. A pressure cooker doesn't lose liquid to evaporation the way a slow cooker does, so this smaller amount of broth is plenty to build steam and a rich gravy.
Nestle the roast back on top of the vegetables, seal the lid, and pressure cook on high for 60 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 15 minutes before opening the valve the rest of the way — this keeps the meat from seizing up and staying tough.
Slice or shred the roast, spoon the vegetables and thickened juices over the top, and serve warm.
Pat the roast dry and season all over with salt and black pepper.
Heat a large pot over medium-high and sear the roast on all sides until deeply browned, about 8 minutes total.
Remove the roast and add the onion, carrots, and garlic to the drippings, stirring until the onion softens, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and thyme for 30 seconds, then pour in the beef broth, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom of the pot.

Nestle the roast back into the pot, bring to a gentle simmer, then cover and reduce the heat to low. A stovetop simmer needs to stay low and steady, just like a slow cooker's gentle heat, or the outside of the meat will toughen before the inside is tender.
Simmer covered, turning the roast once or twice, for about 2 hours.
Add the potatoes, tucking them into the liquid around the roast, and continue simmering covered until the potatoes are tender and the roast shreds easily with a fork, about 30 more minutes.
Slice or shred the roast, spoon the vegetables and pan juices over the top, and serve warm.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté and melt the butter. Cook the onion until soft, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the garam masala, cumin, and paprika and toast for 30 seconds, stirring so the spices don't scorch on the hot metal.
Add the chicken thighs, tomato sauce, and salt, stirring to coat the chicken.
Seal the lid and pressure cook on high for 10 minutes, then quick-release the steam.
Open the lid, check that the chicken is tender and cooked through, and stir in the heavy cream until the sauce turns silky and orange-pink.
Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed, then serve over rice or with warm flatbread.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft and golden at the edges, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add the garam masala, cumin, and paprika and toast for 30 seconds, stirring constantly so they don't burn.
Pour in the tomato sauce, add the chicken thighs and salt, and bring to a simmer. Unlike a slow cooker, a stovetop simmer needs watching — keep the heat at a gentle bubble, not a hard boil.
Cover and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through and tender, about 18 minutes.
Stir in the heavy cream and simmer uncovered for 2 more minutes until the sauce turns silky and orange-pink.
Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed, then serve over rice or with warm flatbread.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté and cook the onion until softened, about 3 minutes, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken breasts, white beans, green chiles, chicken broth, cumin, oregano, and salt.
Seal the lid and pressure cook on high for 12 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes before opening the valve the rest of the way.
Lift out the chicken breasts and shred with two forks, then return the shredded meat to the pot.
Stir in the cream cheese until it melts into the broth and the chili turns creamy.
Squeeze in the lime juice, taste for salt, and ladle into bowls.
Warm a splash of the chicken broth in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 4 minutes — using broth instead of oil softens the onion just as well.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, and oregano and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add the chicken breasts, white beans, green chiles, the remaining chicken broth, and salt, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer gently, turning the chicken once, until it shreds easily with a fork, about 20 minutes.
Lift out the chicken, shred with two forks, and return it to the pot.
Stir in the cream cheese until it melts into the broth and the chili turns creamy.
Squeeze in the lime juice, taste for salt, and ladle into bowls.
Toss the pork shoulder chunks with the cumin, oregano, chili powder, salt, and black pepper.
Set up the grill for indirect heat — coals or burners on one side only — and preheat to about 325°F.
Put the seasoned pork, onion, and garlic in a disposable foil pan, then pour the orange and lime juice over the top.

Set the pan on the cool side of the grill, close the lid, and cook low and slow the way a slow cooker would, until the pork pulls apart easily, about 3 hours. Check the coals or burner occasionally to keep the temperature steady.
Shred the pork right in the pan juices, discarding large onion pieces if you prefer.
Spread a portion of the shredded pork directly over the hot side of the grill grates for a couple of minutes per side so the edges crisp and char — the direct heat does what a broiler would.
Serve in tortillas or over rice while the crispy bits are still warm.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté and toss the pork shoulder with cumin, oregano, chili powder, salt, and black pepper directly in the pot along with the onion and garlic.
Pour the orange and lime juice over the pork.
Seal the lid and pressure cook on high for 45 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 15 minutes, then open the valve the rest of the way — this keeps the pork from getting tough.
Lift the pork out of the juices and shred with two forks.

Set the pressure cooker back to sauté, return the shredded pork to the pot in a single layer, and let it sit undisturbed until the edges crisp and brown in the rendered fat, about 8 minutes, stirring once halfway.
Serve in tortillas while the crispy bits are still hot.
Toss the pork shoulder with the cumin, oregano, chili powder, salt, and black pepper.
Place the pork in a large pot with the onion and garlic, then pour the orange and lime juice over the top.

Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook at a gentle simmer, turning the pork occasionally, until it pulls apart easily, about 2 hours 30 minutes. Add a splash of water if the liquid runs low before the pork is tender.
Shred the pork right in the pot juices, discarding large onion pieces if you prefer.
Heat a large skillet over high heat and spread a portion of the shredded pork in a single layer, letting it sit undisturbed until the edges crisp and brown, about 4 minutes.
Serve in tortillas while the crispy bits are still warm.
Season the beef stew meat with salt and black pepper, then toss with the flour until lightly coated.

Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches until the edges darken, about 5 minutes total — this happens on the stove since a slow cooker can't sear, but it's worth the extra pan for the flavor.
Transfer the beef to the slow cooker along with the onion, garlic, carrots, and potatoes.

Stir the tomato paste and worcestershire sauce into the beef broth, then pour it over everything in the slow cooker. Use the full amount of broth here — over many hours a slow cooker loses more liquid to gentle steam than a sealed pressure cooker does.
Cover and cook on low until the beef is fork-tender and the vegetables are soft, about 7 hours (or 4 hours on high if you're short on time).
Taste for salt and black pepper, and serve in deep bowls.
Warm the vegetable broth in a small saucepan over low heat and keep it at a bare simmer nearby — adding warm broth instead of cold keeps the rice cooking at a steady pace.
Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and arborio rice and cook for 1 minute until the grains look glossy and toasted at the edges.

Add a ladle of the warm broth and a pinch of salt, stirring often until the liquid is mostly absorbed. Repeat, adding broth a ladle at a time, until the rice is creamy and tender but still has a slight bite, about 18 minutes total.
Stir in the parmesan cheese until the rice turns creamy. Season with black pepper and more salt if needed.
Spoon into bowls right away while it is still loose and silky.
Place the potatoes in a large pot, cover with water, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Boil the potatoes until just fork-tender, about 12 minutes, then use a slotted spoon to lift them into a colander to cool.
Bring the same water back to a gentle boil, add the eggs, and cook for 10 minutes for firm yolks.
Move the eggs to an ice bath to stop the cooking, then let both the eggs and potatoes cool until just warm.
Peel and chop the eggs. Halve or quarter the potatoes and add both to a large bowl with the celery, red onion, and pickle relish.
Stir in the mayonnaise and mustard. Season with salt and black pepper until it tastes bright and creamy.
Chill for a few minutes if you can, or serve slightly warm — both work.

Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 4 minutes, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds — softening these first keeps the soup from tasting raw after a long slow cook.
Transfer the onion and garlic to the slow cooker along with the canned tomatoes, vegetable broth, basil, sugar, salt, and black pepper.
Cover and cook on low until the tomatoes have broken down and the flavors have melded, about 5 hours (or 3 hours on high).
Blend the soup until smooth with an immersion blender right in the slow cooker, or carefully transfer in batches to a blender.
Stir in the heavy cream, taste for salt, and serve hot with grilled cheese or crackers.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 4 minutes, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the canned tomatoes, vegetable broth, basil, sugar, salt, and black pepper, and bring to a simmer.
Simmer uncovered, breaking up the tomatoes with a spoon, until the flavors deepen, about 20 minutes.
Blend the soup until smooth with an immersion blender, or carefully transfer in batches to a blender.
Stir in the heavy cream, taste for salt, and serve hot with grilled cheese or crackers.
Pat the pork chops dry and rub with olive oil.
Mix the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper, then coat both sides of the chops.
Heat the grill to medium-high, about 400°F, and clean and oil the grates.
Grill the chops over direct heat until good grill marks form, about 4 minutes per side.
Move the chops to a cooler part of the grill, close the lid, and continue cooking until the centers are just opaque and a thermometer reads 145°F, about 6 more minutes.
Rest on a plate for 3 minutes so the juices settle, then serve.
Preheat the oven to 400°F — 25°F hotter than the air fryer setting, since oven heat is less direct.
Pat the pork chops dry and rub with olive oil.
Mix the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper, then coat both sides of the chops.
Arrange the chops on a wire rack set over a baking sheet so air circulates underneath, similar to how an air fryer basket works.
Bake until the centers are just opaque and a thermometer reads 145°F, about 20 minutes, flipping halfway.
Rest on a plate for 3 minutes so the juices settle, then serve.
Preheat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Toss the sweet potato fries with olive oil, then sprinkle on the cornstarch, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper and toss again until evenly coated.
Spread the fries in a single layer with space between them — crowding them steams the fries instead of browning them, which matters even more in an oven than an air fryer basket.
Bake until the edges are browned and crisp, about 25 minutes, flipping halfway through.
Taste and add a pinch more salt while hot, then serve with your favorite dip.
Pat the chicken thighs very dry so the skin can crisp. Rub with olive oil.
Mix the paprika, garlic powder, dried thyme, salt, and black pepper, then season under and over the skin.
Set up the grill for two-zone cooking — hot coals or burners on one side, nothing on the other — and heat to medium, about 375°F.
Place the thighs skin-side down over the hot side and grill until the skin is deep golden and releases easily from the grates, about 8 minutes.
Move the thighs to the cooler side, close the lid, and continue cooking until the thickest part reaches 165°F, about 20 more minutes.
Rest 3 minutes, then serve with a simple salad or roasted veg.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Pat the chicken thighs very dry so the skin can crisp. Rub with olive oil.
Mix the paprika, garlic powder, dried thyme, salt, and black pepper, then season under and over the skin.
Set the thighs skin-side up on a wire rack over a baking sheet so air can reach the underside, the way an air fryer basket does.
Bake until the skin is deep golden and the thickest part reaches 165°F, about 35 minutes.
Rest 3 minutes, then serve with a simple salad or roasted veg.
Preheat the oven to 375°F and line a baking sheet.
Finely chop a few of the mushroom stems. Mix them with cream cheese, parmesan cheese, garlic, breadcrumbs, parsley, salt, and black pepper.
Brush the mushroom caps lightly with olive oil and fill each with the cream cheese mixture, mounding it slightly.
Arrange the mushrooms on the baking sheet and bake until the tops are golden and the mushrooms look juicy, about 18 minutes.
Cool for a minute so the filling sets, then serve warm.
Toss the bell peppers and onion with 1 tablespoon of the olive oil, half the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, and salt.
Heat the grill to medium-high, about 400°F, and set a grill basket directly on the grates to heat up.
Grill the peppers and onion in the basket, stirring occasionally, until they soften and pick up char at the edges, about 10 minutes.
Toss the shrimp with the remaining olive oil and spices, then thread onto skewers so they don't slip through the grates.
Grill the shrimp skewers directly over the heat until pink and curled with light grill marks, about 2 minutes per side.
Warm the tortillas on the edge of the grill for a few seconds per side while the shrimp rests.
Squeeze the lime over everything and pile the shrimp and vegetables into the warm tortillas.
Heat the griddle to medium-high and drizzle 1 tablespoon of the vegetable oil onto one section.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, pour onto the hot section, and scramble until just set, then push to a cool corner of the griddle.

Add the remaining oil to a clear section of the griddle and stir-fry the garlic and frozen peas and carrots until hot, about 2 minutes, using your spatulas to keep everything moving on the flat surface.

Spread the cooked rice across the hot griddle in a thin layer, breaking up clumps with your spatulas, and let it sit undisturbed for a few seconds at a time so it picks up light char before flipping — the wide flat surface browns rice better than a pan can.
Push the vegetables and eggs into the rice, pour the soy sauce and sesame oil over everything, and toss together with the spatulas.
Scatter the green onions over the top, taste for salt, and serve hot straight off the griddle.

Return the chicken and add the dijon mustard, lemon juice, garlic, bay leaf, and chicken broth.
Lock the lid, seal, and cook on high pressure for 12 minutes, then quick-release.
Remove the bay leaf and season with salt and pepper.

Grind the peanuts and mix with the paprika, cayenne, garlic powder, ginger, and salt for a suya spice.
Toss the beef sirloin with the vegetable oil and most of the spice, then thread onto skewers.
Heat the oven to 450°F and set a rack over a baking sheet.
Roast the skewers, turning once, until charred at the edges and cooked to your liking, about 12 minutes.
Sprinkle with the remaining suya spice and serve with the sliced onion.
Cook the onion in a dry skillet until soft and reduced, then transfer it to the slow cooker.
Add the butter, garlic, ginger, berbere, and tomato paste and stir into the onion.
Nestle in the chicken thighs and pour over the chicken broth.
Cover and cook on low until the chicken is very tender, about 6 hours.
Add the hard-boiled eggs for the last 20 minutes to warm through.
Finish with the lemon juice and salt.
Press sauté and cook the onion until soft and reduced, about 8 minutes.
Add the butter, garlic, ginger, berbere, and tomato paste and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken thighs and chicken broth.
Lock the lid, seal, and cook on high pressure for 15 minutes, then quick-release.
Stir in the hard-boiled eggs to warm through, then finish with the lemon juice and salt.
Whisk the lime juice, orange juice, garlic, half the cilantro, cumin, olive oil, salt, and jalapeno into a marinade.
Marinate the skirt steak for at least 20 minutes.
Heat a cast-iron skillet over high heat until smoking — a screaming-hot pan gives the same char as a grill, indoors.
Sear the steak, turning once, until crusted outside and cooked to 145°F for medium, about 8 minutes.

Scatter the remaining cilantro over the top and serve with lime.
Toss the cherry tomatoes, olives, capers, garlic, and olive oil together.
Preheat the air fryer to 380°F for 3 minutes.
Season the cod with salt and pepper and the oregano and set it in the basket with the tomato mixture around it.
Air fry until the cod flakes easily and reaches 145°F and the tomatoes burst, about 10 minutes.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon and a scatter of parsley.
Grease the slow cooker insert and add the quinoa, plant milk, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt.
Cover and cook on low until the quinoa is tender and creamy, about 6 hours — perfect to wake up to.
Stir in the maple syrup and vanilla extract.
Top with sliced banana and berries.
Rinse the quinoa and add it to the pressure cooker with the plant milk, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt.
Lock the lid, seal, and cook on high pressure for 2 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes.
Stir in the maple syrup and vanilla extract.
Spoon into bowls and top with sliced banana and berries.
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with parchment paper.
Toss the sweet potato, onion, and bell pepper with the olive oil, cumin, paprika, and salt on the pan.
Roast until the sweet potato is tender and browned at the edges, about 25 minutes, stirring once — the oven crisps more surface than a skillet.
Add the black beans and roast for 5 minutes more to warm through.
Scatter cilantro over the top and serve.
Peel the ripe plantains and slice them on a diagonal about half an inch thick.
Toss the slices with the vegetable oil.
Preheat the air fryer to 375°F for 3 minutes.
Air fry, flipping once, until golden and caramelized, about 10 minutes.
Sprinkle with salt while warm.
Place the frozen edamame pods in a microwave-safe bowl with the water.
Cover and microwave on high until bright green and hot, about 4 minutes.
Drain the edamame pods well.
Toss with the sea salt and serve warm.
Peel the green plantains and slice them into very thin rounds.
Toss the rounds with the vegetable oil.
Preheat the air fryer to 360°F for 3 minutes.
Air fry in a single layer, shaking often, until crisp and pale gold, about 12 minutes.
Sprinkle with salt while hot and let cool to crisp up.
Cut the pineapple into thick spears or rings.
Stir the brown sugar and cinnamon together, then brush the pineapple with the melted coconut oil and coat it with the cinnamon sugar.

Air fry, turning once, until caramelized and golden at the edges, about 10 minutes.
Finish with a squeeze of lime.
Add the purple corn, water, cinnamon, and cloves to the pressure cooker.
Lock the lid, seal, and cook on high pressure for 20 minutes, then quick-release — pressure pulls the deep purple color from the corn far faster than simmering.
Strain out the corn and spices, returning the purple liquid to the pot.
